ArduPlane Stratos

Formerly ArduPlane Custom. Same firmware and release tracks; v2.1 is the first release under the new name.

📖 Easier to read: this README as a page with an outline on the ArduPilot Tools site, with every section one click away.

🛠️ One firmware, two release tracks. Every release is built from this branch for two groups of boards:

Track Boards What's compiled in
full-v* F7 / H7, 2 MB flash every hardware backend upstream ships, plus this fork's additions
light-v* 1 MB F4 the same fork feature set, with rarely-used GPS / RC / battery / rangefinder / CAN backends stripped to fit

Both tracks carry the identical fork feature set and share one git hash; the light configuration switches on automatically for 1 MB boards (see Building). ⬇ Download: grab the newest build for your board from the Releases page (every version, newest first — the current releases are full-v2.1 and light-v2.1).

A curated fork of ArduPlane, rebased onto upstream ArduPlane 4.7.2 (tag Plane-4.7.2, commit fb77356789). This branch carries a set of additions and behaviour changes on top of stock 4.7.2, mostly ported from shellixyz's classic 2022 fork and the maintained successor at ArduCustom/ardupilot, plus a few additions originating in this fork.

If you fly stock ArduPlane and don't recognise the param names in this document, you are on the wrong firmware — go to ardupilot.org instead.

📋 Read first — your GCS won't describe this fork's parameters. Mission Planner and QGroundControl ship the upstream parameter metadata, so every parameter this fork adds (and every fork-added bit on FLIGHT_OPTIONS, RC_OPTIONS, OSD_OPTIONS, …) shows up with a blank description, no value list, and no bitmask checkboxes. The parameter still works — your GCS just doesn't know what it is. Use this fork's own docs instead of guessing:

  • Full parameter reference — every parameter this firmware exposes, with descriptions, units and ranges.
  • Bitmask calculator — tick the bits you want and copy out the integer to paste into your GCS (or paste a value back to see which bits are set).

One set covers both release tracks.

Those two, plus the transmitter-side scripts (TECS tuning helper, Yaapu Course Hold pack), are collected under Documentation and tooling. The browser tools are also on one page: ArduPilot Tools.

What's new in v2.1

Everything below is on both tracks unless it says "full only".

Area Change Details
Name ArduPlane Custom is now ArduPlane Stratos. The boot banner reads ArduPlane V4.7.2 Stratos v2.1; parameters, release tracks and branch names are unchanged Firmware version string
Base Rebased onto ArduPlane 4.7.2 (v2.0 was on 4.7.1). A bug-fix release: no parameter renames. Most visible fix: a flight controller mounted upside down or rotated (AHRS_ORIENTATION not 0) no longer waits minutes for "Roll/Pitch inconsistent" after power-up What ArduPlane 4.7.2 brought in
Flight Adaptive pitch trim (RCx_OPTION 254, PTCH_TRIM_SPD / PTCH_TRIM_OFS): pitch trim scheduled on airspeed, learned in a few straight legs; KFF_THR2PTCH is ignored while the curve is active Adaptive pitch trim
Flight Servo auto-trim also works in Course Hold, under the same rules as FBWA: SERVO_AUTO_TRIM 1 (once), 2 (continuous) or the RCx_OPTION 200 switch. With 0 and the switch low, Course Hold never trims Auto-trim improvements
Flight FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21 handover message starts with "Takeoff complete", so Yaapu voices it Bit 21
VTOL Q_FS_EKF_HOLD (off by default): after an EKF failsafe, refuse switching from a VTOL mode to a fixed-wing mode for N seconds, so a forward transition can't start on a bad height estimate Q_FS_EKF_HOLD
RC 32 RC channels (RC_32CH_ENABLE, off by default), RC17_–RC32_OPTION 32 RC channels
RC mLRS RC over MAVLink (radio_rc_channels) on every board, light 1 MB F4 included; stock needs a 2 MB board. Channels 17–32 stay steady with mLRS 1.4.04's mixed 16/32-channel frames mLRS MAVLink RC
Head tracking Head tracking from the VTX gimbal port (SERIALn_PROTOCOL 51) for goggles that don't send it over MSP; one UART can also drive a CADDX gimbal; MSP head tracking wins when both arrive Gimbal-port head tracking
Head tracking Short or malformed MSP head-tracker frames are dropped
OSD ADS-B traffic warning: the OSDx_ADSB element flashes inside OSD_W_ADSB_DIST (and optionally OSD_W_ADSB_ALT). Full only Traffic warning
Radar RADAR_OSD_MODE 1 shows the nearest peer instead of cycling. A peer without a GPS fix (sending 0,0) is no longer drawn with a distance to 0,0 Radar OSD element
Boards Four new tone-buzzer variants: AtomRCF405NAVI-Buzz, CoreWingF405WingV2-Buzz, CoreWingF405MiniV2-Buzz (light) and TBS_LUCID_H7_OEM-Buzz (full) play the full pitched tunes on a passive buzzer wired to the LED pad, instead of the single-pitch beeps of the stock buzzer output. They give up only the LED pad's own output; the stock boards still ship alongside for anyone who wants it Tone-buzzer variants
Boards CoreWing F405 Wing V2 and Wing Mini V2 (CoreWingF405WingV2, CoreWingF405WMiniV2, light): new in ArduPlane 4.7.2, shipped on upstream's own board definitions CoreWing F405 Wing V2 / Wing Mini V2
Boards MatekF405-Wing-PWM10 (light): MatekF405-Wing-bdshot with the LED pad back as PWM output 10 instead of relay 1 Light track

Why flash this instead of stock ArduPlane 4.7.2?

Everything stock ArduPlane 4.7.2 does still works underneath — this fork only adds on top (both variants carry the identical feature set; they differ only in which hardware backends are compiled in). If you fly long-range or FPV fixed-wing, these are the additions most worth flashing for. Each group links to its full reference below.

🖥️ A much richer FPV / long-range OSD

The single biggest visible difference from stock — dozens of new elements aimed at efficiency and situational awareness:

  • Efficiency in Wh/km or mAh/km, resting cell voltage (sag-free pack health at a glance), and battery used since arming.
  • End-of-flight stats grid (distance, time, peak values) plus a persistent max-flight-time record.
  • Angle of attack, demanded vs actual airspeed, attitude-corrected rangefinder AGL altitude, longitudinal/lateral/vertical G, peak roll/pitch rates, auto-flap %, input throttle %, live tuning param name + value, and loiter radius.
  • Under/over-speed warning flashes, one/two-decimal polish on speed, vertical speed and attitude, and a shortenable plus code home locator.
  • ADS-B traffic in the goggles (full-track boards): the nearest aircraft from an ADS-B receiver, with direction arrow, distance and height relative to you — iNav-style. Upstream only shows ADS-B traffic on the GCS map. From v2.1 it flashes when traffic comes inside a distance you set (OSD_W_ADSB_DIST).

→ OSD additions

🛟 Wind-aware autoland & a real failsafe glide-in

Protecting the airframe when the link drops or the battery runs marginal:

  • LAND_WIND_BIAS auto-picks the upwind DO_LAND_START, with LAND_WIND_DIST capping how far the wind bias may reach and LAND_WIND_STRICT turning that cap into a hard fence — so a battery-marginal RTL doesn't fly away to a distant wind-aligned approach.
  • Emergency-landing state machine on RC failsafe: instead of orbiting home until the battery dies, it sinks to a glide altitude, aligns into wind, glides down and disarms. Fully parameterised (FS_ELAND_*).
  • RTL Autoland Commit (RCx_OPTION 251): hold over home until you flip a switch, then commit to the landing sequence. On RC failsafe it waits RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY seconds (default 30) before committing, so a brief dropout can't trigger the landing.

→ Emergency landing · RTL & failsafe behaviour

🚀 Hand-launch & arming ergonomics

Built for throwing a wing off your hand safely:

  • TKOFF_THR_IDLE idles the prop once armed and the stick is raised — a clear "armed and ready" cue in the palm — with TKOFF_IDL_DELAY to pause before the ramp.
  • Pre-launch audio cues and a lost-vehicle alarm on failsafe.
  • Arm-switch safety: an in-flight disarm cuts throttle and drops to FBWA rather than killing the servos and dropping the plane out of the sky. ARMING_MODE_SW auto-switches to TAKEOFF/AUTO after arming.
  • End the climb in FBWB (FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21) instead of loitering out at TKOFF_DIST — control the moment the plane is up, with altitude still held for you until you move the sticks.
  • End a VTOL transition in FBWB (FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 18) — on a quadplane, finish the forward transition holding altitude instead of being left in FBWA with the throttle stick still where you left it.
  • FLTMODE_EXT gives a full 12 flight-mode positions on one channel.

→ Arming & takeoff · Flight modes

🎛️ Tune and take control in the air

  • Knob-tunable pitch trim (PTCH_TRIM_DEG, plus Q_TRIM_PITCH on VTOL) and three switchable tuning sets (TUNE_PARAM/PARAM2/PARAM3) — retune live without a laptop.
  • Adaptive pitch trim (v2.1, RCx_OPTION 254) — airspeed-scheduled pitch trim, learned by the aircraft itself in a few straight legs. FBWA holds height hands-off much better across the speed range (SITL: climb with speed halved with a pitot, cut by two thirds without); without a pitot, FBWB / CRUISE speed changes also lose about 20 % less height. With a pitot the TECS modes gain nothing.
  • Move sticks to cancel auto launch: nudge pitch or roll during an automatic takeoff and the plane drops to FBWA so you can abort a bad launch — iNav-style, active only while the takeoff is running.
  • Throttle stick sets target airspeed in RTL/LOITER/CIRCLE/AUTO, plus pilot loiter radius + direction control in LOITER/RTL, and in the TAKEOFF-mode loiter once the climb finishes.
  • Extra modes: Course Hold (heading hold) and Auto Trim as a mode.

→ Pitch trim & tuning · Manual airspeed · Cancel auto launch

📡 Long-range extras

  • Peer-aircraft radar (iNav Radar / FormationFlight) — see other aircraft on your OSD.
  • Richer telemetry: CRSF relative altitude + link quality, MSP/DJI numeric-attitude fix, wind in km/h, vehicle UID.
  • mLRS RC over MAVLink on every board (v2.1) — radio_rc_channels works on the light 1 MB F4 builds too; stock ArduPilot needs a 2 MB board or a custom build. Up to 32 channels with RC_32CH_ENABLE.
  • Expanded battery monitoring: Wh accounting, cell count/voltage, and capacity-remaining plus low/critical thresholds feeding the OSD readouts.

→ Peer-aircraft radar · Telemetry · Battery monitoring

🎥 Head-tracked FPV gimbal (MSP)

  • Point your gimbal with your head — head-tracker angles come from the goggles over the MSP DisplayPort link and drive the mount (pan/tilt/roll). Drives any gimbal ArduPilot supports on the full (H7) build — Siyi, SToRM32-serial, Topotek, Viewpro, CADDX (CADDXFPV GM-series), servo, …
  • Switch to enable head tracking (RCx_OPTION 252) and to centre + FPV-lock it (253). You can also use the Walksnail Goggles X Gimbal Lock feature to switch the gimbal to FPV mode.
  • POI lock with head tracking (RCx_OPTION 186) — lock the gimbal onto the spot you are looking at, look around freely, flip back to head tracking. Available on every board with gimbal support, including the light F4 boards.
  • Goggles that don't send head tracking over MSP (v2.1) — the FC can read it from the VTX's gimbal port instead (one extra wire, SERIALn_PROTOCOL 51). Same switches, same gimbals.

→ Walksnail Headtracking via MSP and Serial Gimbal · Head tracking from the gimbal port

🆙 On the ArduPlane 4.7 base

From v2.0 the fork sits on ArduPlane 4.7 instead of 4.6.3 (v2.0 on 4.7.1, v2.1 on 4.7.2), so everything 4.7 brings is underneath too — a leaner EKF3, fence margin warnings, EKF lane switching, gimbal lock switches, MAVLink signing and many driver fixes. 4.7 also renamed and rescaled a number of upstream parameters; saved values are converted on first boot, but hand-loaded .parm files are not. 4.7.2 adds bug fixes only (no renames), most visibly for boards mounted upside down or rotated.

→ Upgrading from v1.1 (ArduPlane 4.6.3 base)

What ArduPlane 4.7.2 brought in

v2.1 carries every 4.7.2 change; nothing was dropped. These are the ones that matter for planes and VTOLs. Changes for Copter, Sub, Linux boards and the build tools are left out of this list.

What changed in 4.7.2 Who notices In Stratos v2.1
Upside-down or rotated flight controllers (AHRS_ORIENTATION not 0): the gyro calibration at boot no longer strips the board rotation from the accelerometer. On 4.7.1 the backup attitude estimate could start up to 180° off and block arming with "Roll/Pitch inconsistent" for minutes Boards mounted inverted or sideways All boards
Dead reckoning without a pitot: when EKF3 starts treating the wind as fixed (GPS lost, no airspeed sensor) it no longer flags itself unhealthy for a moment, which could hand navigation to DCM and show a jump in position No-pitot planes that lose GPS All boards
OSD heading, home and wind arrows use the VTOL-view heading Tailsitters All boards. Stratos keeps its own rounding of roll and pitch on the OSD, and its radar and ADS-B arrows use the same heading
Harmonic notch, quintuple option (INS_HNTCH_OPTS bit 6): the filter always has room for whole harmonics Quintuple-notch users All boards
EKF3 drag fusion with GPS yaw no longer waits for compass alignment Dual-GPS (moving-baseline) yaw All boards
Optical flow: the sign of the terrain height used for flow scaling is fixed Optical flow over terrain Where optical flow is built
Compasses: QMC5883P is now on 1 MB boards; IIS2MDC fixed and enabled Those compasses All 22 fleet boards include both
Barometers: BMP581 reads corrected data; BMP390 is reset at start-up to clear an old configuration Boards or modules with these baros Full builds only: the light builds don't include these two drivers
LSM6DSV IMUs: KakuteH7 / KakuteH7 Mini and Pixhawk6X support them, and the LSM6DSV heater is now driven Those boards All boards where the IMU is used
MAVLink: long status messages sent in several parts by another component (gimbal, companion computer) are put back together again GCS logs and messages All boards
Follow (FOLL_*, used by the plane follow script): the target is dropped when FOLL_SYSID changes, and the automatic target detection is gone Plane follow script users Full builds (light builds have no scripting)
New boards upstream: CoreWing F405 Wing V2 and Wing Mini V2, CUAV-X25-MEGA, GPilot P1, Lectron Pi5, NWBLUE_PROH757 Owners of those boards In the source and buildable, but not in the Stratos release fleet

The full upstream list is in ArduPlane's release notes.

Most additions are opt-in via parameters and change nothing until you enable them — but a few defaults do differ from stock. Skim Behaviour changes vs upstream before your first flight.

Building

Identical to upstream. From a configured WSL / Linux toolchain:

./waf configure --board <your-board>
./waf plane

The branch builds clean for every board in the release fleets; SITL builds and runs cleanly.

Full or light is picked by the board's flash size

There is no separate light branch. AP_CUSTOM_LIGHT, defined in libraries/AP_HAL/AP_HAL_Boards.h as HAL_PROGRAM_SIZE_LIMIT_KB <= 1024, switches on the light configuration for boards with 1 MB of flash:

  • RC input: CRSF, SBUS, FPORT, FPORT2 and IBUS only
  • GPS: u-blox only, one receiver
  • airspeed: analog and MS4525 only; battery monitor: analog and ESC telemetry only
  • rangefinder: Benewake (TF02 / TF03 / TFmini / TFmini Plus) only
  • one compass; no DroneCAN or PiccoloCAN; no ICE
  • a Light suffix on the version string

Everything else — including every fork feature — is identical. Larger boards and SITL build the full configuration. A hwdef can still override any single setting (for example define AP_ICENGINE_ENABLED 1).

Firmware version string

Mavlink AUTOPILOT_VERSION (the banner that shows up in MissionPlanner on connect, and in arduplane --help) is built up as:

ArduPlane V<x.y.z> Stratos <FORK_VERSION>[ Light] (<git-hash>)

For example:

ArduPlane V4.7.2 Stratos v2.1 (1a2b3c4)        # 2 MB board (full track)
ArduPlane V4.7.2 Stratos v2.1 Light (1a2b3c4)  # 1 MB board (light track)

The hash is the commit the release was built from; the release notes print it, and the release tags (full-v2.1 / light-v2.1) point at it.

The upstream ArduPlane V4.7.2 prefix is kept so GCS tools that parse the upstream version string (MissionPlanner, MAVProxy, autotest scripts) keep working. FORK_VERSION lives in libraries/AP_Common/AP_FWVersionDefine.h — bump it on each release. The Light suffix is added automatically on 1 MB boards (AP_CUSTOM_LIGHT, see above). Both tracks of a release are built from the same commit, so they show the same hash. Up to v1.1 the brand in the string was ArduCustom, and v2.0 used Custom.

What this fork adds

Flight modes

Course Hold (mode 26)

A heading-hold mode similar to CRUISE but the locked target is your ground track instead of the magnetic heading. Useful when you want the plane to fly a straight line over the ground in wind. Roll stick input still rolls the plane; releasing returns to the locked course.

  • Enable: set any FLTMODE_n = 26
  • Tunable: CRUISE_YAW_RATE (deg/s — how fast the locked course rotates when you hold roll input)

⚠️ Mode 26 is also upstream's AUTOLAND. ArduPlane 4.7 added an AUTOLAND flight mode numbered 26. This firmware compiles AUTOLAND out (MODE_AUTOLAND_ENABLED 0) and keeps Course Hold at 26 — wind-aware landing is done with RTL_AUTOLAND + DO_LAND_START instead (see RTL & failsafe behaviour). Ground stations that build their mode list from the vehicle (AVAILABLE_MODES, e.g. QGroundControl) show COURSE HOLD; Mission Planner and MAVProxy use their own stock 4.7 tables and may label mode 26 "AUTOLAND". The firmware runs Course Hold either way — only the label is wrong. To teach MAVProxy the right name, edit mode_mapping_apm in modules/mavlink/pymavlink/mavutil.py.

📡 Yaapu telemetry — showing and announcing Course Hold and Auto Trim

Stock Yaapu's plane-mode table stops short of mode 26, so Course Hold shows as a blank chip with no audio cue, and Auto Trim (mode 27) has no entry at all, which stops the Yaapu script. Drop-in files fix both — Tools/yaapu-coursehold/ in this repo, and attached to every release as plane.lua + coursehold.wav + autotrim.wav so you don't need to clone anything.

On an EdgeTX widget install (e.g. RadioMaster TX16S):

  1. Replace Yaapu's plane.lua under WIDGETS/yaapu/ with the one provided — this adds CourseHold at index 27 and AutoTrim at index 28 (Yaapu indexes flight_mode + 1, so 27 = our mode 26 and 28 = mode 27).
  2. Delete the plane.luac next to it; it's a compiled cache and will regenerate.
  3. Copy coursehold.wav and autotrim.wav into WIDGETS/yaapu/sounds/en/ (your language folder if not English).

⚠️ Right name but no sound? That's the WAV being in a folder Yaapu doesn't read — the two things are looked up separately, so the HUD text can work while the audio silently doesn't. The sound folder depends on which Yaapu build you run:

Build the WAVs go in
EdgeTX widget (TX16S) WIDGETS/yaapu/sounds/en/
OpenTX / Horus script SOUNDS/yaapu0/en/
FrSky Ethos scripts/yaaputelemetry/audio/en/

None of these is EdgeTX's own SOUNDS/en/ folder, which is for Special Functions and unrelated to Yaapu.

The same plane.lua works for the Yaapu GCS desktop tool — see Tools/yaapu-coursehold/README.md for that and for recording your own cue.

Auto Trim (mode 27)

Flies like Course Hold (locked ground-track heading, pilot trims roll/pitch by stick) and simultaneously runs the servo auto-trim loop in the background. Use it to push small trim into the saved servo trims while still actively flying — no need to land between adjustments. Exiting the mode stops the loop.

  • Enable: set any FLTMODE_n = 27 (or use FLTMODE_EXT slots 7..12)
  • When it trims: only while roll and pitch demands are within ±7° and ground and air speed are both 8 m/s or more, so turns and slow flight are skipped. Trims are saved every 10 s.
  • SERVO_AUTO_TRIM decides when it stops: 0 keeps trimming until you leave the mode; 1 stops by itself once every surface has settled (SAT_FINISHTHRESH, "Servo auto trim finished") and sets the parameter back to 0 — the plane keeps flying Auto Trim, it just stops trimming; 2 trims in every eligible mode anyway, so the mode adds nothing. See Servo auto-trim.
  • The mode shares Course Hold's CRUISE_YAW_RATE + FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 20 (yaw-stick steers locked heading) behaviour because it inherits from ModeCourseHold.
  • Upstream ArduPlane 4.7.2 does not use mode number 27. As with Course Hold, GCSs that read AVAILABLE_MODES show it by name (AUTO TRIM).
  • Yaapu: install the fork's plane.lua first — stock Yaapu has no entry for mode 27 and its script stops when you switch into Auto Trim. The pack also adds an autotrim.wav cue; see Yaapu telemetry.

RC aux switch entries (Plane)

Plane's RCx_OPTION enum gains five entries — two so the pilot can put autotrim and autotune on momentary aux switches without burning a FLTMODE_n slot, plus the RTL Autoland Commit gate, VTOL AutoTrim and Adaptive Pitch Trim:

  • RCx_OPTION = 17 — AUTOTUNE Mode. Switches into Plane's AUTOTUNE flight mode (mode 8) on switch HIGH. Upstream had this enum value wired only for Copter; the fork extends it to Plane. This is flight-mode entry, distinct from RCx_OPTION = 107 (FW_AUTOTUNE), which toggles the autotune loop without changing flight mode.

    ⚠️ Stay in autotune until each axis reports Finished. Leaving earlier (either option) puts the old gains back for any axis that has not found both its D and its P limit — upstream behaviour, but easy to miss. Progress shows as RollD: x → RollP: x → Roll: Finished, and the same for pitch. Fly sharp, full-stick inputs on both axes, held about 1 s and reversed, for several minutes; a tune flown mostly on roll leaves pitch unfinished and discarded.

  • RCx_OPTION = 200 — Servos Auto Trim. Starts the servo auto-trim accumulator on switch HIGH (with a clean prepare so it doesn't resume from a previous run) and stops it on LOW. Stays in whatever flight mode you're already in (FBWA / CRUISE / etc.) — it does not force AUTO_TRIM mode. GCS prints "Servos auto trim started" / "stopped" as it toggles. Slot 200 matches mf0o's port, so saved RCx_OPTION = 200 params from mf0o-based builds keep working. (The legacy 2022 fork used slot 162 for the same option; re-save the param if you're migrating from the old fork.)
  • RCx_OPTION = 182 — VTOL AutoTrim (new in v2.0). Learns the hover-only Q_TRIM_ROLL / Q_TRIM_PITCH in QHOVER; Copter's option number for the same idea. See VTOL AutoTrim.
  • RCx_OPTION = 251 — RTL Autoland Commit. Gates the RTL → landing jump when RTL_AUTOLAND = 1: the plane holds at the home loiter until you flip this switch HIGH, then commits to DO_LAND_START. See RTL & failsafe behaviour for the full behaviour and the RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY failsafe grace timer.
  • RCx_OPTION = 254 — Adaptive Pitch Trim (new in v2.1). A 3-position switch: LOW off, MIDDLE on, HIGH learns the airspeed trim curve. See Adaptive pitch trim.

FLTMODE_EXT — 12-position FLTMODE_CH

Default 0 keeps the upstream 6-position behaviour bit-for-bit. Set 1 and ArduPlane reads the FLTMODE_CH PWM as a 12-bin selector instead of 6 — useful when your radio's source for FLTMODE_CH is an OpenTX/EdgeTX multi-position switch with more than 6 positions.

  • Bins are 75 µs wide starting at 1126 µs (1126/1201/.../1876).
  • Positions 1..6 use the existing FLTMODE1..6 params (no change).
  • Positions 7..12 use new params FLTMODE7..FLTMODE12 (default FBWA each).
  • Stable digital RC links recommended (SBUS / CRSF / ELRS). PPM / analogue PWM is not recommended — 75 µs bins are too tight for jitter typical of analogue links.

Originally Stavros Korokithakis 2021 (e8ff5a8dfd), forward-ported through ArduCustom; this re-port adapts to upstream 4.6.3's RC_Channel-based mode-switch refactor.

Arming & takeoff

Arm-switch safety — in-flight disarm cuts throttle, doesn't disarm

If the pilot moves the arming aux switch to "disarm" while the plane is flying, the firmware will not disarm. Instead it:

  1. Cuts the throttle output (every mode, including MANUAL).
  2. If the current mode is auto-throttle (RTL / LOITER / AUTO / CRUISE / FBWB / etc.), switches to FBWA so the pilot can fly the plane down by stick.
  3. Updates the OSD flight-mode chip to show the disarmed symbol so the pilot has a visual confirmation.
  4. Latches emergency_landing on for the duration of the cut, so if an RC failsafe fires before the plane is on the ground the failsafe path stays in FBWA rather than reverting to RTL into terrain. The flag is restored to its pre-cut value on rearm.
  5. Defers the real disarm until is_flying() reports false. Once the plane has actually landed (update_is_flying_5Hz sees it below the speed/airspeed thresholds), the deferred disarm completes automatically.

While the throttle-cut state is active, moving the arming switch back to "arm" rearms instantly with no checks — it just clears the throttle-cut and restores the pre-cut mode (if the auto→FBWA bump happened). This is the V10.0 ArduCustom safety pattern: the throttle cut is a softer-than-disarm action and you can recover from it.

GCS messages: - Throttle cut by arm switch — at the moment the cut fires (fixed-wing or VTOL with throttle stick at zero) - Disarm prevented — VTOL with throttle stick still raised; the motors are still spinning, drop the stick to let them stop - Rearmed — when the arm switch goes back to "arm" mid-cut

VTOL / quadplane behaviour: in a VTOL mode (QHover, QLoiter, QRTL, QLand, etc.) the firmware does not switch the plane to FBWA on cut. The motors only stop once the throttle stick reaches zero, so the pilot can land vertically by holding throttle down. Raising the stick again before the arming switch flips back keeps the motors live so the pilot can fly out. The throttle output servo channels (k_throttle, k_throttleLeft, k_throttleRight) are also forced to zero on the cut side as belt-and-braces in case a twin-motor path bypasses the standard throttle suppression.

Caveats: - SITL retains the upstream behaviour so autotest still passes — the in-flight disarm guard is gated by CONFIG_HAL_BOARD != HAL_BOARD_SITL. - The deferred disarm completes silently via disarm_if_requested() in update_is_flying_5Hz. It does the standard disarm() path so log close + AP_Notify state + everything else still runs. - MAVLink and rudder-stick disarm requests in-flight are still rejected outright (no throttle-cut path).

ARMING_MODE_SW — auto mode switch after arming

After arming, wait ~3 seconds, then automatically switch to the selected mode. Lets a single aux-switch arm and launch a TKOFF/AUTO mission with no second mode-switch action.

  • ARMING_MODE_SW = 0 — disabled (default)
  • ARMING_MODE_SW = 1 — switch to TAKEOFF after arming
  • ARMING_MODE_SW = 2 — switch to AUTO after arming

⚠️ v1.1 / v1.2 builds: reboot after a cancelled launch. On those builds, re-arming after a launch was cancelled mid-throw could make this automatic TAKEOFF entry fire the launch on the ground. Fixed in v2.0; see Re-arming after a cancelled launch.

TKOFF_THR_IDLE — pre-launch idle throttle

Hold a small throttle the moment the pilot raises the stick while the plane is sitting in pre-launch suppressed-throttle state (AUTO with current nav cmd = NAV_TAKEOFF, or TAKEOFF mode). Lets you idle an ICE engine before launch or spin an electric motor at low RPM ready to fly.

  • TKOFF_THR_IDLE = 0 (%) — disabled (default)
  • TKOFF_THR_IDLE = 25 — hold 25 % throttle when stick raised
  • TKOFF_IDL_SRATE = 50 (%/s) — slew rate while ramping up to the idle value (0 = instant snap up)

Snap-to-zero when the stick is dropped is instant regardless of slew rate. THR_SUPP_MAN = 1 still takes precedence (continuous manual passthrough) — set THR_SUPP_MAN = 0 to let idle throttle take over.

ℹ️ Since v2.0 TKOFF_THR_IDLE is upstream's parameter. ArduPlane 4.7 added its own TKOFF_THR_IDLE; this firmware uses that parameter for the fork's stick-gated idle, so there is still exactly one TKOFF_THR_IDLE. It holds a whole percent (integer) — a fractional value saved by v1.1 or earlier is rounded on the first boot of v2.0. TKOFF_IDL_SRATE and TKOFF_IDL_DELAY are unchanged.

TKOFF_IDL_DELAY — pause before idle ramp

Optional delay (seconds) between the pilot first raising the stick and the throttle starting to ramp toward TKOFF_THR_IDLE. Mainly useful for ICE engines that want a fixed "warm at idle" pause before being commanded up.

  • TKOFF_IDL_DELAY = 0 (default) — no delay, idle ramp starts immediately on stick-up
  • TKOFF_IDL_DELAY = 5 — hold throttle at 0 for 5 s after first stick-up, then start the idle ramp normally

The timer resets whenever the stick returns to zero or the plane leaves the pre-launch suppressed-throttle state. A GCS text TKOFF idle THR timer started fires when the timer begins.

Pre-launch audio cues

The buzzer/ToneAlarm plays distinct cont tones during the pre-launch sequence so the pilot doesn't have to watch the GCS:

State Tone Meaning
TKOFS_WAITING_TO_RAISE_THROTTLE Rapid triple-beep loop Stick is at zero in pre-launch — raise it to start the idle ramp
TKOFS_WAITING_FOR_IDLE_THROTTLE Rising scale (cdefgab) Stick is up, idle throttle is ramping (or TKOFF_IDL_DELAY timer is still running)
TKOFS_WAITING_FOR_LAUNCH Slow steady beep At idle throttle, waiting for launch detection to fire
TKOFS_IDLE (silent) Default; takeoff sequence not active

Tones loop until the state changes — works the same way pre-arm and EKF-failsafe cont tones do. No parameter to enable; it's automatic whenever TKOFF_THR_IDLE is configured.

Plain GPIO buzzers (v1.1). The table above needs a ToneAlarm output (a pitched buzzer on a PWM/ALARM pin) to play actual tones. Boards with only a plain on/off GPIO buzzer — AtomRCF405NAVI among them — previously got no pre-launch cues at all. They now play the same three states as distinct cadences instead of pitches:

State GPIO buzzer cadence
TKOFS_WAITING_TO_RAISE_THROTTLE Slow lone beeps
TKOFS_WAITING_FOR_IDLE_THROTTLE Medium double-beeps
TKOFS_WAITING_FOR_LAUNCH Fast continuous

The three are deliberately far apart in rhythm so they stay tellable apart by ear on a buzzer that can only be on or off. Nothing to configure — the cues appear automatically on boards that have a GPIO buzzer and no ToneAlarm; boards with a ToneAlarm are unchanged and still play the tones in the first table.

Timing note. The GPIO buzzer enforces a 3.3 s minimum gap between patterns (32 bits × 100 ms). State-change cues bypass that gap so they sound the moment the state changes — otherwise a "ready to launch" cue could arrive up to 3.3 s late, well after a hand launch has happened. The repeat of the launch-ready cue still respects the gap.

Pilot altitude control during TAKEOFF loiter

After the initial climb in TAKEOFF mode, the plane enters a loiter circle around the target waypoint. The pitch (elevator) stick now adjusts altitude during this loiter phase the same way FBW-B does it — pull back to climb, push forward to descend — so the pilot can settle the plane at the right altitude before flipping to AUTO or RTL.

No parameter to enable; behaviour is on whenever TAKEOFF is the active mode and flight_stage is past the initial climb — and whenever the loiter phase runs at all. Set FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21 to skip that phase entirely and hand over in FBWB at the end of the climb instead.

⚠️ Do not assume LOITER behaves the same way. This always-on behaviour is specific to the TAKEOFF loiter. In LOITER mode the same stick gesture does nothing to the target altitude unless FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 12 is set — without it the plane climbs while you hold the stick and sinks back the moment you release. Bit 12 is a fork default from v2.0 on, but upgrades keep whatever FLIGHT_OPTIONS you already had saved.

Since v1.1 the roll and rudder sticks work here too — radius and turn direction, from the ArduCustom PR #180 port. See pilot control of loiter radius and direction. During the climb itself the pitch and roll sticks instead cancel the launch; the two phases never overlap.

🐞 Fixed in v1.1 — stale climb target on airframes with an airspeed sensor. ModeTakeoff::navigate() wrote the pilot-adjustable target altitude back into the loiter waypoint unconditionally, from the moment the mode started — before that value had been seeded off the loiter waypoint. Entering TAKEOFF from FBWB could therefore latch the climb target at ground level, so the plane would level off almost immediately instead of climbing to TKOFF_ALT. Aircraft without an airspeed sensor were unaffected, because their climb is pitch-driven rather than TECS-driven. The write-back is now gated on the altitude having been seeded.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21 — end TAKEOFF in FBWB instead of loitering

New in v2.0. With this bit set, reaching the end of the TAKEOFF climb hands the plane straight to you in FBWB instead of entering the loiter circle. The mode changes, so everything above stops applying: there is no loiter at TKOFF_DIST, no pitch-stick altitude nudging, no radius or direction control — you are flying the aircraft, with a "Takeoff complete - FBWB" message on the GCS and OSD. Yaapu speaks "takeoff complete" for it (it voices any message starting with those words), followed by the FBWB mode announcement.

Photo from v2.0, which showed SWITCHING TO FBWB; from v2.1 the same line reads TAKEOFF COMPLETE - FBWB.

The climb itself is unchanged. TKOFF_ALT, TKOFF_LVL_ALT, TKOFF_LVL_PITCH and the launch-cancel window all behave exactly as they do with the bit clear; only the end of the sequence differs.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21 At the end of the climb
clear (default) loiter at TKOFF_ALT / TKOFF_DIST, still in TAKEOFF mode
set (2097152) switch to FBWB

Useful if you hand launch into a small field and want control the moment the plane is up, rather than watching it circle out to TKOFF_DIST before you can take over. The alternative — cancelling the launch with the sticks — drops to FBWA during the climb and abandons it; this option lets the climb finish first.

ℹ️ Why FBWB. The handover is the moment you are least ready — the plane has just been thrown, it is nose-up at the top of a climb, and your thumbs may not be on the sticks yet. FBWB latches the current altitude as its target the instant it is entered, so doing nothing means straight and level — the aircraft holds the height it finished the climb at until you tell it otherwise.

Pull the throttle stick back to about mid once you have the plane: in FBWB the throttle stick commands target airspeed, not throttle, and it will be sitting near AIRSPEED_MAX straight after the climb. (FLIGHT_OPTIONS bits 1 and 3 change that mapping if you use them.)

⚠️ Not the same as RC_OPTIONS bit 21. Two different parameters in this fork now use bit 21, and both take the value 2097152: RC_OPTIONS bit 21 is the disarm → MANUAL revert, FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 21 is this takeoff handoff. Check the parameter name, not just the bit number.

⚠️ Check TKOFF_DIST against TKOFF_ALT before you use this. The takeoff stage ends at whichever comes first — TKOFF_ALT, or TKOFF_DIST of ground track from the launch point — so a TKOFF_DIST that is short relative to TKOFF_ALT hands you the plane early, at whatever altitude the climb reached by then. Rule of thumb: TKOFF_DIST >= TKOFF_ALT / tan(climb angle), which for a typical ~16 deg climb means TKOFF_DIST >= 3.4 x TKOFF_ALT. SITL with TKOFF_ALT 120 / TKOFF_DIST 150 handed over at 151 m and only 44 m up. This is upstream takeoff behaviour, not something bit 21 adds — with the bit clear the same setup starts its loiter at 44 m — but the handoff makes it obvious where the loiter used to hide it.

⚠️ The switch is suppressed under RC failsafe. FBWB is still a pilot-flown mode, so if the link is down at the end of the climb (or a long failsafe is pending), the plane keeps the legacy loiter and lets the failsafe action decide. You only get FBWB when there is a transmitter to fly it with.

VTOL transition

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 18 — end a VTOL transition in FBWB instead of FBWA

New in v2.0. On a quadplane, leaving a VTOL mode (QLOITER, QHOVER, QSTABILIZE) for FBWA starts a forward transition: the lift motors keep holding the aircraft up while the forward motor builds speed, and once the airspeed estimate has passed AIRSPEED_MIN and held for Q_TRANSITION_MS the lift motors shut down and you are flying on the wing — still in FBWA, because FBWA is the mode you selected.

With this bit set, completing the transition also hands the aircraft to you in FBWB, with a "Transition done, switching to FBWB" message on the GCS and OSD.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 18 When the transition completes
clear (default) stay in FBWA
set (262144) switch to FBWB

The transition itself is untouched. Q_ASSIST_SPEED, Q_ASSIST_ANGLE, Q_TRANSITION_MS, Q_TRANS_FAIL and the airspeed threshold all behave exactly as they do with the bit clear; only the mode you are left in differs.

ℹ️ Why FBWB. The same reasoning as the takeoff handover. FBWB latches the current altitude as its target the instant it is entered, so doing nothing means straight and level. In FBWA sticks-centred is only wings-level at zero pitch demand, and the throttle goes to wherever the stick is sitting — which straight after a transition is usually still well up, where it was driving the acceleration.

Pull the throttle stick back to about mid once you have the plane: in FBWB the throttle stick commands target airspeed, not throttle. (FLIGHT_OPTIONS bits 1 and 3 change that mapping if you use them.)

ℹ️ Only a transition out of a VTOL mode triggers it. The switch fires on the completion edge, and only when the mode you came from was a VTOL mode. Without that second condition a Q_ASSIST episode later in the same FBWA flight — assistance engaging when you get slow, then clearing again — would look identical to a finished transition and would quietly move you to FBWB when no transition had taken place.

⚠️ Your mode switch will disagree with the aircraft. The switch is still sitting on FBWA while the plane is flying FBWB. Moving the switch away and back to FBWA gives you FBWA again — that is the way back if you want it, but it also means an idle flick of the switch undoes the handover.

⚠️ Suppressed under RC failsafe. FBWB is a pilot-flown mode, so if the link is down when the transition completes (or a long failsafe is pending), the aircraft stays in FBWA and lets the failsafe action decide.

ℹ️ No airspeed sensor is fine. The transition threshold uses the AHRS airspeed estimate, so this works on ARSPD_TYPE 0 airframes exactly as it does with a pitot — the estimate is simply noisier, which affects when the transition finishes, not what happens afterwards.

ℹ️ Why bit 18 and not 17. Upstream allocates FLIGHT_OPTIONS bits upward from the lowest unused one — 4.7 took 15 and 16, so 17 is where its next addition will land. The fork's bits allocate downward from the bit-24 MAVLink ceiling (19–24 arrived that way from ArduCustom), so this one takes 18 and leaves 17 as a one-bit buffer between the two. Checked against 4.7.0, 4.7.1-beta1 and 4.8.0-dev: none of them uses a bit above 16.

Flight-tested on a KakuteH7-Wing VTOL: QHOVER → FBWA, and FBWB was announced as the transition completed.

Q_FS_EKF_HOLD — no forward transition right after an EKF failsafe (v2.1)

Why: in a VTOL position mode (QLOITER, QHOVER, QRTL…) an EKF failsafe ("EKF variance") switches to QHOVER, or QLAND in AUTO. Upstream then lets the pilot switch straight to a fixed-wing mode. That starts a forward transition: forward motor at full throttle, low down, while the lift motors hold height on the same estimate that just failed. On a tester's quad-X VTOL the failsafe fired at 9 m, the pilot switched QHOVER → FBWB half a second later, and under the acceleration the GPS vertical speed read a 15 m/s climb. The EKF believed it was above its target height, the lift motors throttled down to near zero and it flew into the ground.

What it does: for Q_FS_EKF_HOLD seconds after the EKF failsafe was last active, a change from a VTOL mode to a fixed-wing mode requested by the RC mode switch, an RC aux switch or the GCS is refused with EKF failsafe: FBWB denied for 7s (the time left if the EKF stays good). Everything else still works:

  • Changes between VTOL modes are allowed. QSTABILIZE in particular is the bail-out when the EKF height is wrong, because you control the lift throttle directly.
  • Failsafe actions are not blocked (RC, battery, GCS failsafe).
  • The time counts from when the EKF is last bad, not from when the failsafe fired: once it has fired, the hold keeps watching the EKF in every mode and restarts the count while it is still over FS_EKF_THRESH. That matters because upstream stops checking as soon as the aircraft is out of a VTOL position mode, and the failsafe itself switches to QHOVER, which isn't one. Disarming resets it.
  • If Q_ASSIST_ALT is set, the hold applies only below that height (the same height source as the assist). With Q_ASSIST_ALT 0 it applies at any height.
  • A refused RC mode switch is not retried. Move the switch again once the hold is over.
Parameter Default Meaning
Q_FS_EKF_HOLD 0 (off, stock behaviour) Seconds, 0–60. Suggested 10

It does not help when the EKF is wrong but confident. In the crash above the EKF's own error scores went back to normal 1 s into the transition and stayed there while it descended. The fix for that is in the setup: EK3_SRC1_VELZ 0 (don't use GPS vertical speed), GPS_AUTO_CONFIG 1, and transitions from at least 20 m.

Pitch trim & tuning knob

PTCH_TRIM_DEG is now knob-tunable

PTCH_TRIM_DEG can be assigned to the in-flight tuning knob via TUNE_PARAM = 59 (TUNING_PITCH_TRIM). The OSD OSDx_TUNED_PN / OSDx_TUNED_PV elements (see OSD section) display the live value during the tune.

  • TUNE_PARAM = 59, TUNE_CHAN = <RC channel>, TUNE_RANGE = <max-multiplier>

REQUIRED: PTCH_TRIM_DEG must be non-zero before you engage the knob. AP_Tuning's knob math is purely multiplicative around the parameter's current value — the knob sweeps [seed / TUNE_RANGE, seed * TUNE_RANGE]. If the seed is exactly 0, every multiplier is still 0, so the knob appears dead and the value will not change no matter where you turn it.

Workflow: 1. Set PTCH_TRIM_DEG to a small non-zero value (e.g. 0.5, or -0.5 to explore nose-down) via the GCS before engaging the knob. 2. Re-centre the knob (selector switch low, <500 ms hold) so the new seed becomes the mid-point. 3. To cross zero or flip sign, re-seed manually and re-centre — the multiplicative scheme cannot cross zero on its own.

The same caveat applies to Q_TRIM_PITCH via TUNE_PARAM = 92.

Three switchable tuning sets — TUNE_PARAM / PARAM2 / PARAM3

Two extra tuning-set slots and a new RC aux function to switch between them in flight, so you can run three different tuning workflows from a single 3-position switch without landing to change TUNE_PARAM.

  • TUNE_PARAM (existing) — active when the selector aux switch is low
  • TUNE_PARAM2 (new) — active in the middle position
  • TUNE_PARAM3 (new) — active in the high position
  • Assign RCx_OPTION = 250 (TUNE_PARAM_SELECT) to a 3-position switch
  • All three default to 0 (disabled); set any/all to a non-zero tuning ID to enable

When the switch moves, the new set re-centres the knob and the GCS announces the active parameter — no reboot needed.

Faster tuning selector timing

The tuning selector channel (TUNE_SELECTOR) used to need full seconds of hold time per action. Now:

Action Old New
Save tune > 5000 ms > 3000 ms
Debounce window < 200 ms < 50 ms
Re-centre 200–2000 50–500
Next parameter 2000–5000 500–3000

Interactions feel responsive in fractions of a second instead of multi-second holds.

ATT log uses trim-corrected pitch target

The logged ATT.DesPitch channel now has PTCH_TRIM_DEG subtracted out, so log replay matches the value the controller actually targets in horizon-relative terms.

Adaptive pitch trim — airspeed schedule, learned in flight (RCx_OPTION = 254)

New in v2.1.

Why it matters. A plane needs a different pitch attitude to fly level at each speed: nose higher when slow, lower when fast. PTCH_TRIM_DEG is a single number, so it is right at one speed only. At every other speed the flight controller holds the wrong attitude as "level":

  • In FBWA, Course Hold and Auto Trim, hands-off flight climbs when you add throttle and sinks when you slow down, so you keep correcting with the pitch stick.
  • In FBWB, CRUISE, AUTO and the other TECS modes, TECS has to carry a standing pitch correction to hold height, and find it again after every speed change.

Adaptive pitch trim replaces the single number with a curve: three airspeeds (PTCH_TRIM_SPD1..3), each with its own extra trim (PTCH_TRIM_OFS1..3) on top of PTCH_TRIM_DEG. The aircraft can learn the curve itself from a few straight legs, or you can set it by hand or from a log. The offset is added where PTCH_TRIM_DEG goes, after the flight mode has computed its pitch demand. It is off during takeoff, landing and VTOL.

It does not measure or control angle of attack: there is no AOA vane or AOA estimate, only pitch trim scheduled on airspeed. "Adaptive Pitch Trim" is the name used everywhere in the firmware (the RCx_OPTION 254 switch, the Adaptive trim … messages and the PTCH_TRIM_* parameters).

How it compares with PTCH_TRIM_DEG alone and with KFF_THR2PTCH. All three are added to the same pitch target, after the flight mode has computed its demand (ArduPlane/Attitude.cpp):

pitch target = mode demand + PTCH_TRIM_DEG + curve offset (airspeed)
                           + KFF_THR2PTCH × throttle % / 100
PTCH_TRIM_DEG only KFF_THR2PTCH (stock ArduPlane) Adaptive pitch trim (this fork)
What it adds One fixed angle An angle in proportion to throttle: 100 % throttle adds KFF_THR2PTCH degrees An angle read from a 3-point curve against airspeed, on top of PTCH_TRIM_DEG
What it follows Nothing Throttle Airspeed (synthetic airspeed without a pitot)
Right at One speed, the one it was trimmed at Steady level flight, where throttle tracks speed. In a climb or a glide the throttle is different at the same speed, so the trim shifts although the speed hasn't changed Every speed on the curve, whatever the throttle is doing
Shape Flat A straight line in throttle Three points, straight lines between them, so it can bend
How you set it By hand, at cruise By hand, trial and error; documented range ±5° Learned in flight from a few straight legs, by hand, or from a log
Near the stall No change Low throttle changes it, whatever the speed Stall taper: never raises the nose below 1.25 × AIRSPEED_MIN
Fit on four real flight logs (against the pitch each log flew level) Level pitch changed by 2.5–3.7° across each log's speed range; a single trim can be off by up to that much 0.42–1.38° RMS at best, and only with values of −12 to −17, far outside its ±5 range 0.30–0.39° RMS

They work together like this: PTCH_TRIM_DEG stays the base and should be right at cruise; the curve adds its offset on top. KFF_THR2PTCH is faded out while the curve is active, since both do the same job, and applies again whenever the curve is off (see KFF_THR2PTCH is ignored while the curve is active further down).

What you gain. Measured in SITL on the v2.1 build, no wind. FBWB speed changes are a 10 m/s step, 10 runs with a pitot and 6 without.

Where With a pitot Without a pitot
FBWA hands-off, throttle changed (Course Hold and Auto Trim use the same pitch path) Clear gain. Height gained over an 80 s throttle sweep: 31.7 → 18.4 m (42 % less). Climb at 50–100 % throttle: 21–44 → 16–22 m/min Clear gain. 23.7 → 10.8 m (54 % less). Climb: 20–43 → 8–14 m/min
FBWB, CRUISE, AUTO, LOITER, RTL, steady Height hold unchanged: TECS already holds it. Its standing pitch correction shrinks from −0.87° to −0.21° at full speed Same: −0.80° → −0.07°
Same modes, after a speed change Small cost, not noticeable: 0.1–0.2 m more height change (up 5.48 → 5.61 m, down 3.25 → 3.46 m) Gain: about 20 % less (up 1.00 → 0.83 m, down 0.86 → 0.66 m)
Takeoff, landing, VTOL Off Off

The simulated plane's level pitch changes by only about 0.9° across its speed range. On four real flight logs it changed by 2.5–3.7°, so expect larger effects, both gains and costs, on a real airframe. On those four logs the curve matched the real level-flight pitch to within 0.30–0.39° (RMS). Stock ArduPlane's KFF_THR2PTCH managed 0.42–1.38° at best, and only with values of −12 to −17, far outside its documented ±5.

Why the two setups differ: with a pitot TECS ignores the trim, so it simply cancels the offset in its own pitch demand, slightly late as the speed changes (a 0.02–0.04° pitch difference, enough for 0.1–0.2 m). Without a pitot TECS sets throttle from the pitch measured against the trim (AP_TECS.cpp, _update_throttle_without_airspeed), so a trim that matches level flight at every speed is used by the throttle loop as well; this is the likely reason speed changes improve there.

Which setup benefits:

Setup Recommendation
Pitot, flown mostly in TECS modes Not needed. KFF_THR2PTCH 0 and no curve does as well: in the same step test a best-fit KFF_THR2PTCH (−1.69) and the curve both stayed within ±0.25 m of using neither
Pitot, flies FBWA Use the curve, PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 = AIRSPEED_CRUISE
No pitot Use it in all modes, PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 not below the trim-throttle speed (see Without a pitot)

Caveats:

  • The curve belongs to one weight and balance. Level pitch at a given speed depends on wing loading and CG. Learn at your normal take-off weight; after a big change in payload, battery or CG, learn again or check hands-off FBWA at a few speeds.
  • Set the basics first. The offsets are measured against PTCH_TRIM_DEG, so get that right at cruise first. Tune TECS before learning, and run any transmitter TECS helper with the switch LOW (see below).
  • Gusty air. In SITL turbulence (10 m/s wind, SIM_WIND_TURB 2), steady height hold was slightly looser with the curve: 0.87 → 0.95 m RMS with a pitot, 0.97 → 1.06 m without (8 and 9 of 12 runs). Small, but in the wrong direction. Learning also goes slowly in gusts.
  • Without a pitot it runs on the wind estimate. Synthetic airspeed is GPS speed corrected by the wind estimate; an error there shifts the whole curve along the speed axis, and the stall taper uses the same estimate.
  • No new stall protection. The taper only stops the curve from raising the nose near AIRSPEED_MIN. FBWA still lets you slow into a stall exactly as before.
  • KFF_THR2PTCH is ignored while the curve is active, since both do the same job (details below).
  • The numbers above are from a simulated plane. They show the direction and rough size of the effects, not what your airframe will do.

TECS_INTEG_GAIN, TECS_PTCH_DAMP and TECS_TIME_CONST only change how fast TECS reaches the level pitch; TECS_PTCH_FF_K looks similar but only applies while gliding. Tune TECS first, then learn the curve.

Parameters (PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 = 0 turns the whole feature off):

Param Unit Meaning
PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 / SPD2 / SPD3 m/s three airspeeds, increasing
PTCH_TRIM_OFS1 / OFS2 / OFS3 deg (±10) trim added to PTCH_TRIM_DEG at each speed

Between the points the offset is interpolated in a straight line; outside them it stays at the end value. The offset only applies when armed and flying in normal flight: not during takeoff or landing, and not in VTOL or assisted flight. It changes smoothly (about a 1 s time constant).

Stall taper. From 1.25 × AIRSPEED_MIN down to AIRSPEED_MIN the offset fades to the least nose-up of the three offsets, so slowing towards the stall never raises the nose.

Sample only: these numbers are one aircraft's and are not a recommendation; they will not suit yours. The curve was fitted from a flight log (PTCH_TRIM_DEG 2, AIRSPEED_MIN 16). The blue dots are the pitch that log flew level at each airspeed; hollow dots had under 30 samples and were left out of the fit. The solid line is the trim the firmware holds as level; the dashed line is PTCH_TRIM_DEG alone. Between the points the trim follows a straight line, and above 24.5 m/s it stays at point 3. In the shaded band (16–20 m/s, AIRSPEED_MIN to 1.25 × AIRSPEED_MIN) the stall taper fades it to the least nose-up offset (−1.08°), so the nose drops slightly as the plane slows instead of rising. Point 1 (19.5 m/s) sits inside that band, so the taper overrides it there; the explorer flags this as CHECK. Your own curve comes from a learn flight, or from a log. To see it, load your .param or .bin into the Adaptive Pitch Trim Explorer.

The switch (RCx_OPTION = 254, 3-position):

Switch Effect
LOW off (the learned curve is kept)
MIDDLE on
HIGH learn; moving off HIGH fits the curve and saves it

With no switch assigned, the curve is used whenever one exists. The position at boot only chooses on or off; it never starts a learn.

Learning a curve: 1. Put the switch HIGH (Adaptive trim learn: fly level FBWB/CRUISE). A switch already HIGH at boot does not learn: move it off HIGH and back. 2. In FBWB or CRUISE, fly straight and level at 4–5 different speeds, about 4–5 m/s apart, holding each speed for 5–10 s. Progress shows every 10 s as Adaptive trim learn: N speeds. 3. Move the switch off HIGH — one move, no need to go back to HIGH. The curve is fitted and saved, and printed as speed/offset pairs, for example Adaptive trim: 14.5 +2.1 18.5 +1.0 22.5 +0.2. Move to MIDDLE, not LOW: both save, but LOW also turns the curve off. It needs at least 3 speeds spanning 3 m/s. With fewer (or if the fit fails) the GCS shows Adaptive trim: N speeds (need 3 over 3m/s), nothing is saved and the old values stay.

Every move to HIGH starts a new learn run and discards the samples collected so far (the saved curve is untouched until that run is saved).

How to fly the learn legs. The learner never reads the sticks; it samples the aircraft 10 times a second and keeps a sample only when all of these hold:

Check Limit
Roll within ±5°
Vertical speed under 0.5 m/s up or down
Airspeed change under 0.5 m/s per second (filtered)

A 1 m/s airspeed band counts as one learned speed after 30 kept samples (about 3 s of steady flight). So the legs are hands-off on pitch, not on throttle:

  • Pitch stick centred. In FBWB the pitch stick commands a climb or descent, and anything over 0.5 m/s drops the samples.
  • Roll: small heading corrections are fine while the bank stays within 5°. Samples pause while banked further; nothing is lost.
  • Throttle stick sets each speed. With an airspeed sensor the FBWB / CRUISE throttle stick sets the target airspeed between AIRSPEED_MIN and AIRSPEED_MAX (unless FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 3, CRUISE_TRIM_AIRSPEED, is set: then it holds AIRSPEED_CRUISE). Set it, then let the speed settle: samples are rejected while it is still changing. Without a pitot see below.
  • Turns are free. Banked flight is just skipped, so fly a leg, turn around and come back at the same speed: the samples for that speed keep adding up across legs.
  • Calm air. Gusts push the vertical speed and airspeed rate past the limits, so on a bumpy day the counts climb slowly; fly longer legs rather than more speeds.

Setting a curve by hand (no switch needed):

  1. Turn the curve off while you measure. With a switch, put it LOW. Without one, set PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 to 0 (the other five values are kept). A fresh install is already off: all six default to 0. While the curve is on, the displayed pitch also has the offset removed, so readings taken then are wrong.
  2. Check how your display shows pitch. By default the pitch you see has PTCH_TRIM_DEG subtracted, so a plane level at its trim attitude reads 0°. Two FLIGHT_OPTIONS bits turn that off and show the raw pitch instead:
Where you read pitch Bit Value
OSD, and passthrough / MSP telemetry on the radio (Yaapu, TECS helper) 9 512
Mission Planner / GCS HUD 8 256

The fork default (FLIGHT_OPTIONS 4096) has both clear. 3. Measure three speeds in FBWB or CRUISE, where TECS holds altitude so the pitch it settles on is the level-flight pitch. Pick a slow, a middle and a fast speed you actually fly, about 4–5 m/s apart, with the slow one above 1.25 × AIRSPEED_MIN (below that the stall taper takes over). At each speed fly straight, wings level and holding altitude for 5–10 s, and note the airspeed and the pitch. 4. Work out each offset. If the bit for your display is clear, OFS = displayed pitch. If it is set, OFS = displayed pitch − PTCH_TRIM_DEG. The offsets should fall as speed rises; if one doesn't, measure that leg again. 5. Enter the values, PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 last. Set SPD2, SPD3 and OFS1–OFS3 first, then SPD1. The curve switches on as soon as SPD1 > 0 and SPD1 < SPD2 < SPD3, so entering SPD1 last keeps a half-entered curve from going live. Doing this on the ground is simplest; in flight the offset fades in over about 1 s. 6. Check it. With the curve on (switch MIDDLE, or no switch), fly FBWA hands-off at each speed: the plane should hold altitude, and the displayed pitch should read about 0° when level.

Param Value
PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 / SPD2 / SPD3 slow / middle / fast airspeed (m/s)
PTCH_TRIM_OFS1 / OFS2 / OFS3 offset at each speed (deg, positive nose up, ±10)

To turn a hand-set curve off later without a switch, set PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 to 0; put the old value back to turn it on again.

Setting a curve from logs (no OSD needed). Fly the same legs, then read the dataflash .bin instead of a display. Plot these on one time axis:

Field Use
CTUN.As (m/s) airspeed — the same airspeed_EAS() value the learner uses
ATT.Pitch (deg) real aircraft pitch, nothing subtracted
ATT.Roll (deg) keep stretches within ±5°
XKF1.VD (m/s, the core in use: XKF1.C), or TECS.dh keep stretches under 0.5 m/s; TECS.dh is only logged in TECS modes
CTUN.AsT airspeed source: 1 pitot, 2 / 3 synthetic (DCM / EKF3), 0 no new estimate (drop)

Do not use CTUN.Pitch (logged with PTCH_TRIM_DEG and the current curve offset already subtracted) or ATT.DesPitch (the target, trim included). Because ATT.Pitch is the real pitch, the curve does not need to be off while flying the legs, and the FLIGHT_OPTIONS display bits do not matter.

  1. Find stretches of 3 s or more where CTUN.As is flat, ATT.Roll stays within ±5° and XKF1.VD within ±0.5 m/s (the learner's own checks).
  2. Note the mean CTUN.As and mean ATT.Pitch of each.
  3. OFS = mean ATT.Pitch − PTCH_TRIM_DEG, with PTCH_TRIM_DEG read from the log's PARM values. This is the same formula the learner saves. The offsets should fall as speed rises.
  4. Enter them as in step 5 above, PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 last.

A scatter of ATT.Pitch against CTUN.As, using only samples that pass the roll and climb checks, shows the level-flight curve as a band to read three points from.

With a pitot, CTUN.AsT should read 1 throughout. The pitot is only used while ARSPD_USE is 1 and the sensor is healthy; stretches with 2 or 3 used synthetic airspeed and belong to the no-pitot case.

Without a pitot (AsT 2 or 3) the method is the same, with three differences: - A wind-estimate error shifts the whole curve along the speed axis. Fly a few circles first, fly each speed upwind and downwind and average the pair. If the two disagree by more than about 1 m/s, the wind estimate is off and that pair is unreliable. - No points below the trim-throttle speed (the speed the plane flies at TRIM_THROTTLE): keep PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 at or above it, see Without a pitot below. FBWB / CRUISE cannot fly slower anyway. - FBWA legs count from logs. ATT.Pitch is the real pitch in any mode, so a stretch where you held altitude by hand is as good as a TECS-held one, as long as XKF1.VD stays within ±0.5 m/s and the speed is steady — useful if you don't fly FBWB, still at or above the trim-throttle speed. The in-flight learner cannot use these: it only samples in FBWB and CRUISE.

KFF_THR2PTCH is ignored while the curve is active. It is stock ArduPlane's throttle-based version of the same idea: it adds KFF_THR2PTCH × throttle % / 100 degrees to the pitch target in every stabilised mode. The learned curve already lowers the nose as speed rises, so applying both would make that correction twice. When the curve takes over, KFF_THR2PTCH fades out over the same ~1 s as the curve fades in, and the first time this happens after boot with a non-zero value the GCS shows Adaptive trim on: KFF_THR2PTCH ignored. Whenever the curve is off (switch LOW, no curve set, no airspeed estimate, takeoff, landing, VTOL) KFF_THR2PTCH applies as normal, so you can keep your tuned value for those cases. STAB_PITCH_DOWN is not affected: it only lowers the nose when you pull the throttle back in FBWA, for the glide.

Tuning TECS with a transmitter helper (for example the TECS tuning helper): run it with the switch LOW. Those helpers read pitch from telemetry, which has the trim removed, so with the curve active every pitch they capture (TECS_PITCH_MAX / MIN, STAB_PITCH_DOWN) would be shifted by the offset at that speed. Tune TECS first, then learn the curve.

Without a pitot it uses ArduPilot's synthetic airspeed (GPS ground speed corrected by the wind estimate). That works, but a wind-estimate error shifts the curve along the speed axis. Learn on a calm day, fly a few circles first, and fly each speed both upwind and downwind. Without a pitot, TECS also sets throttle from the pitch measured against the trim, so in FBWB, CRUISE and AUTO the curve changes throttle as well: with an accurate curve level flight reads as trim at every speed and throttle stays near TRIM_THROTTLE. For the learn legs this also means the throttle stick does not set a target airspeed: with THROTTLE_NUDGE on, the stick above mid only adds throttle on top of TRIM_THROTTLE (toward THR_MAX), and below mid it does nothing, so the slowest leg is the trim-throttle speed.

That is also the lowest PTCH_TRIM_SPD1 to use without a pitot. Below SPD1 the curve holds OFS1, so slow flight behaves as it does today. Without a pitot the plane only flies slower than that with the throttle pulled back (descents, FBWA throttle-back), where STAB_PITCH_DOWN is lowering the nose and a curve's extra nose-up would partly cancel it, and the stall taper near AIRSPEED_MIN would rest on the synthetic estimate. Don't lower TRIM_THROTTLE or use FBWA legs to get points below it.

Costs about 2.9 KB of flash on a 1 MB F4 board.

RTL & failsafe behaviour

RTL_LVL_RLL_LMT — separate roll limit for the initial climb

During RTL's initial climb to RTL_CLIMB_MIN, the roll limit is reduced to this value (deg) to keep the plane stable as it gains altitude. After the climb phase the normal ROLL_LIMIT_DEG applies.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 22 — RTL_CLIMB_FIRST_ONLY_IN_FS

Without this bit, RTL always climbs to RTL_CLIMB_MIN first before heading home. With the bit set, the climb-first behaviour applies only during RC failsafe — a normal pilot-triggered RTL skips straight to navigation.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 23 — ALLOW_GLIDING_IN_AUTO_THR_MODES

With this bit, pulling the throttle stick below THR_DZ in any auto-throttle mode except TAKEOFF and AUTO triggers the TECS gliding path: throttle is forced to 0 and pitch takes over airspeed entirely (TECS speed weighting goes to 2.0, so height control is given up). Releasing the throttle restores auto-throttle on the next tick.

Which airspeed it glides at depends on the mode. GUIDED, THERMAL, AVOID_ADSB and QRTL take the AIRSPEED_MIN glide target in calc_airspeed_errors(). LOITER, CRUISE, FBWB, RTL and CIRCLE never reach that branch, because the throttle stick already owns their target airspeed — and at sub-THR_DZ stick the default and CRUISE_TRIM_THROTTLE (bit 1) mappings land on AIRSPEED_MIN anyway, so the result matches.

⚠️ The exception is bit 3, CRUISE_TRIM_AIRSPEED. It pins the target to AIRSPEED_CRUISE at any stick position, so bit 3 + bit 23 at zero throttle glides at cruise speed — a noticeably faster and steeper descent than the AIRSPEED_MIN glide this section otherwise describes.

⚠️ THR_DZ (default 4%) does double duty: it is the throttle output deadzone in servos.cpp as well as the gliding stick threshold here. Raising it to stop an ESC creeping also widens the stick band that triggers a glide.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 12 — FBW-B style loiter altitude control (upstream)

Not a fork addition, but documented here because the fork's own pitch-stick altitude features sit either side of it and the asymmetry catches people out.

In LOITER, pitch-stick altitude control needs two things:

Param Value Why
FLIGHT_OPTIONS 4096 (bit 12) — default in this fork since v2.0 "Enable FBWB style loiter altitude control"
STICK_MIXING non-zero, not VTOL_YAW — this fork defaults to FBW ModeLoiter::update() gates on stick_mixing_enabled()

Upstream defaults FLIGHT_OPTIONS to 0, so on stock ArduPlane both of these are off. This fork ships both on, so LOITER altitude control works out of the box.

⚠️ Upgrading from v1.1 or earlier? Changing a default only affects fresh parameter storage. Your saved FLIGHT_OPTIONS carries over untouched, so you still need to add 4096 by hand — same as the STICK_MIXING change in v1.1.

⚠️ Without bit 12 the pitch stick still moves the plane — and that is the trap. It falls through to ordinary stick mixing, which adds a temporary offset to nav_pitch_cd. The aircraft climbs while you hold the stick, then TECS returns it to the original loiter altitude the moment you let go. It looks like altitude control that "forgets" the new altitude, when in fact no altitude command was ever issued.

With the bit set, update_fbwb_speed_height() owns the pitch stick and calls set_target_altitude_current() when the stick returns to centre, so the new altitude is latched and held. FBWB_CLIMB_RATE (default 2.0 m/s) sets how fast the stick moves the target, and the result is clamped by any altitude fence and by CRUISE_ALT_FLOOR.

Contrast with the fork's own two: RTL needs bit 24, while the TAKEOFF loiter needs no parameter at all. Three modes, three different enable conditions — LOITER is the only one relying on an upstream option.

FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 24 — RTL_MANUAL_ALT_CONTROL

With this bit, RTL hands altitude control to the pilot's pitch stick via the FBW-B controller while outside of RC failsafe — push to climb, pull to descend — the same way altitude works in FBWB/CRUISE. The L1 controller still flies the plane home; only the vertical axis is under the pilot. Useful when you want to RTL but choose a different return altitude than ALT_HOLD_RTL without leaving the mode.

The instant RC failsafe fires (or you clear the bit mid-flight), RTL snaps back to its normal climb-to-ALT_HOLD_RTL behaviour cleanly: prev_WP_loc is reset to the current position so TECS doesn't get a sudden altitude jump.

Interactions: - RTL_ALT_HOME is suppressed while manual control is active — the descend-to-home-altitude logic doesn't fight the stick. - RTL_CLIMB_MIN / CLIMB_BEFORE_TURN's initial-climb bump is skipped — TECS isn't pushed to climb when the pilot already owns altitude. - Pitch stick mixing is bypassed (the FBWB path is the sole consumer of the pitch stick), so deflection isn't applied twice.

⚠️ Bit relocated from upstream-fork bit 20 to bit 24 in this rebase because upstream 4.6.3 took bit 20 for the unrelated COURSE_HOLD_HEADING_CONTROL_WITH_YAW_STICK feature. Update your FLIGHT_OPTIONS saved value when migrating from the 2022 fork: 1<<20 becomes 1<<24.

RTL Autoland Commit (RCx_OPTION 251) — hold at home, commit on your command

With RTL_AUTOLAND = 1 the plane normally flies home and then jumps straight into the nearest DO_LAND_START landing sequence. Assign RCx_OPTION = 251 to a two-position switch and that jump becomes pilot-gated: the plane holds at the home loiter (circling) until you flip the switch HIGH, then commits to the landing sequence. This lets you loiter over the field and pick the moment to land, and it defers the wind-biased DO_LAND_START selection (see LAND_WIND_BIAS) until the wind estimate has settled.

Behaviour at a glance (with RTL_AUTOLAND = 1 and the switch assigned):

Switch (RCx_OPTION 251) RC link What the plane does
LOW / hold OK Circles the home loiter indefinitely, waiting for you. GCS: RTL: holding, AUTOLAND switch to land
HIGH / commit OK Commits immediately — GCS RTL autoland: commit, RTL → AUTO, flies DO_LAND_START
LOW / hold RC failsafe, RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY > 0 Keeps circling home, then commits after RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY s (timed from reaching the loiter). GCS: RTL autoland: FS, committing in <n>s
LOW / hold RC failsafe, link recovers before the timer expires Timer resets, gate re-engages → back to holding for you
LOW / hold RC failsafe, RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY = 0 Commits immediately (pre-v1.0 behaviour)
HIGH / commit RC failsafe Already committed before the link dropped → lands
Unassigned (any) any No hold — exactly stock ArduPlane (commits per RTL_AUTOLAND on reaching home)

RTL_AUTOLAND = 2 (go directly to the landing sequence) never loiters at home, so it is never gated by this switch — only RTL_AUTOLAND = 1 is.

RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY — failsafe grace timer (default 30 s). During RC failsafe you can no longer flip the switch, so the plane would otherwise commit to the landing immediately. RTL_AUTOLAND_DLY keeps it circling home for this many seconds (counted from when it settles at the home loiter) before committing — long enough that a brief dropout or a single-frame RC glitch can't trigger the landing. If the link recovers inside the window the gate re-engages and the plane goes back to holding for you; GCS shows RTL autoland: FS, committing in <n>s when the timer starts. Set 0 to commit immediately on failsafe (the pre-v1.0 behaviour). Has no effect when the commit switch is unassigned or already in the commit position.

Why this exists: on a real flight a ~0.4 s ELRS dropout (with the switch still in hold) dropped the gate and committed the landing. The grace timer makes transient link glitches harmless while still guaranteeing the plane lands if the link is genuinely gone.

Lost-vehicle audio alarm during RC failsafe

Once armed in RC failsafe, the lost-vehicle alarm fires. Reuses the existing notify channel; no new param.

Mission restart on AUTO if not flying

If you switch to AUTO before takeoff and the mission's first non-jump item is a NAV_TAKEOFF, the mission restarts at item 1 each time you enter AUTO from a non-flying state. Prevents accidentally resuming a mid-mission item after a failed launch.

LAND_WIND_BIAS — pick the upwind DO_LAND_START

Upstream picks the nearest DO_LAND_START whenever ArduPlane needs to autoland — RTL autoland, fence breach, battery failsafe, or a MAV_CMD_DO_LAND_START from the GCS. In wind, the nearest landing is frequently the downwind one.

LAND_WIND_BIAS (default 0 = upstream behaviour preserved) shifts the selection toward the landing whose final approach faces into the wind. Each candidate is scored as

score = distance * (1 - LAND_WIND_BIAS * cos(approach_heading - wind_from))

where cos returns +1 for a perfect headwind approach (multiplier 1 - LAND_WIND_BIAS, so it counts as shorter) and -1 for a perfect tailwind approach (multiplier 1 + LAND_WIND_BIAS). The lowest-scoring candidate wins. LAND_WIND_BIAS = 1 lets a direct-tailwind 500 m approach lose to a direct-headwind 1000 m approach; 0.3 is a gentler tilt that still breaks ties in favour of upwind landings.

Example with LAND_WIND_BIAS 0.5 and the wind from 200°. Stock ArduPlane would fly to #24, the nearest at 522 m. The fork scores #12 lower (781 × 0.53 = 414 against 522 × 0.83 = 433) because its approach faces the wind, so the plane flies the extra 259 m and lands into wind. The tailwind approach #18 scores 1837. The GCS shows DO_LAND_START 12 (upwind, nearest was 24). To try other winds and positions, use the LAND_WIND_BIAS Explorer.

The approach heading for each DO_LAND_START is derived from the bearing toward the next NAV_* waypoint in the mission — typically the first leg of the descending approach. If no following nav cmd can be found, that candidate is scored on distance alone.

Falls back to nearest-distance (the upstream behaviour) when: - LAND_WIND_BIAS = 0 (any value <= 0) - AHRS wind estimate magnitude is below 1 m/s (unreliable on a pre-takeoff plane, or a GPS-only build before the plane has turned enough for the estimator to settle) - A candidate's approach heading cannot be derived

When wind-bias changes the choice, a DO_LAND_START N (upwind, nearest was M) GCS line is sent next to the standard Landing sequence start text, so you can see the bias actually fired in flight logs.

Note on airframes without an airspeed sensor (any variant): ArduPlane's wind estimator needs the plane to turn to converge when there is no pitot. Straight-line flight just after takeoff may not produce a usable estimate, so the fallback keeps selection nearest-distance until a turn or two has populated the estimator. Airframes with a working pitot get a usable wind estimate much sooner. The light variant is no different from the full variant here — the limitation is in the AHRS estimator, not the build.

LAND_WIND_DIST — why: cap how far the wind bias can reach

The problem it solves: on missions with several DO_LAND_START items spread across a wide area, a strong LAND_WIND_BIAS can pull selection toward a much farther landing just because its approach happens to align with the wind. On a battery-marginal RTL that extra travel can cost you the airframe. LAND_WIND_DIST gives you a distance ceiling: any DO_LAND_START whose start-of-approach sits farther than this many metres from the plane's decision-time position is excluded from selection outright. The wind bias then picks only among the candidates that actually survive the cap.

What "decision time" means depends on RTL_AUTOLAND:

RTL_AUTOLAND When the pick runs Cap effectively measured from
1 (return then autoland) after the plane reaches the RTL loiter point HOME (plane is there)
2 (autoland immediately) as soon as RTL is entered plane's current position
Battery failsafe when the failsafe fires plane's current position
GCS MAV_CMD_DO_LAND_START when the command arrives plane's current position

So for RTL_AUTOLAND=2 and mid-mission failsafes the cap prevents the bias from pulling the plane away from where it already is; for RTL_AUTOLAND=1 it behaves as a home-radius fence, which is what you probably had in mind if you set it up on the bench.

Behaviour cases (LAND_WIND_DIST = 500): - Only one DO_LAND_START within 500 m of the plane → it is picked, tailwind or not. - Multiple within 500 m → LAND_WIND_BIAS decides between them (into-wind approach preferred). - Zero within 500 m → what happens is controlled by LAND_WIND_STRICT (below). Default (= 0) falls back to upstream nearest-across-all; strict (= 1) refuses to autoland.

LAND_WIND_BIAS = 0 still short-circuits the whole feature, so LAND_WIND_DIST has no effect on its own.

LAND_WIND_STRICT — why: make the cap a hard fence

The problem it solves: by default, if LAND_WIND_DIST filters out every candidate, the code falls through to upstream nearest- across-all so the plane still lands somewhere — even if that "somewhere" is far outside the cap you configured. That preserves the failsafe safety net (the plane will always try to land) but partly defeats the point of the cap. LAND_WIND_STRICT lets you opt into a stricter interpretation: when no DO_LAND_START is within the cap, refuse to autoland at all. RTL stays in RTL, the plane keeps loitering at HOME/rally, and the pilot has to intervene.

Values:

LAND_WIND_STRICT Behaviour when zero candidates in cap
0 (default, soft fallback) Fall through to upstream nearest-across-all; the plane still lands, even if the pick is far outside LAND_WIND_DIST. Wind bias is skipped for that one pick.
1 (hard fence) Refuse the autoland. Return false from the picker; RTL stays in RTL, plane loiters at HOME/rally. GCS text: No DO_LAND_START within LAND_WIND_DIST. Pilot must intervene.

When to use each: - = 0 — you want LAND_WIND_DIST to gently guide selection toward nearby landings, but you'd rather the plane always attempt a landing on failsafe (avoid "loiter until battery dies"). This is the safer default for most operations. - = 1 — you have several DO_LAND_STARTs spread across a large area and would rather fly the plane home manually than have it commit to an unexpected 5 km cross-country to satisfy autoland. Common on missions where the "far" landings are spare alternates you don't actually want the autopilot to choose without you.

⚠️ Safety warning: under LAND_WIND_STRICT = 1, a battery failsafe that triggers when no landing is within the cap will not attempt to land — the plane will loiter at HOME/rally until the battery dies and comes down uncontrolled. Only enable strict mode if you are able to monitor the aircraft in flight and take manual control on failsafe. If you cannot guarantee that, leave LAND_WIND_STRICT = 0 and accept the occasional far landing.

Strict mode is silently ignored when LAND_WIND_DIST = 0 (no cap set) or LAND_WIND_BIAS = 0 (whole feature off).

QRTL with RTL_ALTITUDE -1 (fixed in v2.0)

When QRTL is selected far from home, it flies back as a plane: it holds the RTL altitude and only sinks to Q_RTL_ALT on the last stretch, then slows, transitions and lands vertically. Before v2.0 that approach read RTL_ALTITUDE as a plain height. With -1 ("return at the current altitude", which RTL itself handles correctly) it treated the return height as −1 m. So the plane cut the throttle and dropped to Q_RTL_ALT as soon as QRTL was selected, then flew the whole way home that low: 20 km out, that meant about 20 km at Q_RTL_ALT above home, with any rising ground in between even closer. The same code is in upstream ArduPlane since the QRTL approach was added in 2021, and in v1.1.

v2.0 records the RTL altitude when QRTL is entered, so -1 now means the height you selected QRTL at. A positive RTL_ALTITUDE works as before.

Where the descent starts. The plane reaches Q_RTL_ALT at 2 × max(WP_LOITER_RAD, RTL_RADIUS) from home, and starts down early enough to lose the height at 60% of TECS_SINK_MAX:

start = 2·R + AIRSPEED_CRUISE · (H − Q_RTL_ALT) / (0.6 · TECS_SINK_MAX)
R = max(WP_LOITER_RAD, RTL_RADIUS),  H = height when QRTL was entered
capped at 20·R

Example, with WP_LOITER_RAD 150, RTL_RADIUS 90, AIRSPEED_CRUISE 18.7, TECS_SINK_MAX 5 and Q_RTL_ALT 40: entered at 80 m it starts down about 550 m from home, at 100 m about 675 m, at 200 m about 1.3 km. It is at 40 m by 300 m out. In practice the descent starts a little later than the formula, because TECS lags the target.

Q_RTL_MODE does not change this. It is only read by RTL, to decide how RTL hands over to a VTOL landing; a QRTL selected on a switch ignores it. With Q_RTL_MODE 1 RTL switches to QRTL within RTL_RADIUS of home, too close for this approach, so all the height is lost in a hover. With Q_RTL_MODE 2 RTL comes home at RTL altitude, circles down on Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD to Q_RTL_ALT, and only hovers for the last part.

Fork vs upstream, switching to QRTL vs RTL. Example: cruising at 120 m, 1 km from home, RTL_ALTITUDE -1, Q_RTL_ALT 40, Q_RTL_MODE 2, WP_LOITER_RAD -120, RTL_RADIUS 60, Q_FW_LND_APR_RAD 80, AIRSPEED_CRUISE 20, TECS_SINK_MAX 5.

QRTL, v2.0 QRTL, upstream 4.7.1 QRTL, 4.8-dev (master) RTL (all three)
Height on the way home holds 120 m to 773 m out drops to 40 m at once (reached ~680 m out) glides from the entry point holds 120 m to home
Down to 40 m straight line, 773 → 240 m out at up to TECS_SINK_MAX on entry straight line, 1000 → 240 m out spirals down on the 80 m circle over home
Height 500 m out 79 m 40 m 67 m 120 m
Final approach from the direction it arrives same same into the wind (EKF wind estimate)
Lift motors start ~140 m out (airbrake) same same on the into-wind leg near home

4.8-dev's ramp is upstream PR #33786.
