Every board gave up 5–7 KB to v2.1 (the ArduPlane 4.7.2 base plus the v2.1 fork additions); AtomRCF405NAVI-Buzz costs 40 bytes against stock AtomRCF405NAVI. The twelve boards with gimbal support also carry the POI lock switch (about 1.2 KB).

Gimbal mount support is switched back on in these F4 hwdefs. Upstream's minimize_common.inc turns HAL_MOUNT_ENABLED off on flash-constrained boards, which leaves Mission Planner reporting "Invalid channel option" for RCx_OPTION 212/213/214 (mount roll/pitch/yaw). The fork re-enables it with only the servo and CADDX mount backends to save flash.

CoreWingF405WingV2 / CoreWingF405WMiniV2 (STM32F405, 1 MB) are new in ArduPlane 4.7.2 and ship on upstream's own board definitions, unchanged. Serial ports already follow SERIALn = chip UART n: SERIAL1 MAVLink2 (USB extender / wireless module, 115200), SERIAL2 shares its RX with the SBUS input, SERIAL3 VTX, SERIAL4 telemetry, SERIAL5 GPS, SERIAL6 RC input. Outputs: Wing V2 S1–S11 plus the LED pad, bidirectional DShot on 1–4; Wing Mini V2 S1–S9, no bidirectional DShot. CoreWing's definitions already re-enable the gimbal mount (servo + CADDX), and also landing gear and QAUTOTUNE; the fork adds nothing to them. See Wing V2 and Wing Mini V2.

MatekF405-Wing-PWM10 is MatekF405-Wing-bdshot with the LED pad (PA15) back as PWM output 10, as in upstream ArduPilot. The fork's Matek F405-Wing definition uses that pad as the relay 1 pin, which leaves 9 outputs (S9 is the bare solder pad). Output 10 runs on its own timer, so it can use a different PWM rate from 1–9, but it is PWM only — no DShot: its timer's only DMA stream is the one UART3 receive needs, and UART3 (with UART1) is the full-DMA port to use for an ELRS/CRSF receiver. Relay 1 has no default pin on this build (RELAY1_PIN -1); to keep a relay, point RELAY1_PIN at a spare output's GPIO (50–59) and set that SERVOn_FUNCTION to -1. Same board ID, so the .apj flashes over the stock bootloader.

MatekF405-Wing-bdshot and -PWM10 are the canary boards — first to bump the 1 MB ceiling in any future upstream rebase or feature add. Every board on this track is flash-constrained, so nothing here has spare headroom to absorb a regression.

Tone-buzzer board variant: SpeedyBeeF405WING-Buzz

A fork-only variant of SpeedyBeeF405WING that adds a hardware ToneAlarm (pitched-tone) buzzer on the S11 pad (PB15 remapped from the TIM1 PWM group to TIM12_CH2, marked ALARM). This lets the FC play the full ArduPilot tunes — arming, GPS lock, the auto-takeoff/ launch cues above, failsafe — on a dedicated passive buzzer instead of routing them through the DShot ESCs. Cost is one servo output (S11 / channel 11); outputs 1-10 and 12 (WS2812 LED) are unchanged. Board ID is inherited (1106) so the .apj flashes over the stock SpeedyBee bootloader as a normal update. Flash footprint is essentially identical to stock SpeedyBeeF405WING (20.4 KB vs 20.7 KB free at v2.1 — a 0.3 KB difference). Shipped as an extra asset on the light release alongside the other boards above.

A sibling variant, KakuteF4-Wing-Buzz, applies the same idea to the Holybro Kakute F4 Wing — which has no buzzer at all on the stock board. The tone buzzer goes on the WS2812 LED pad (PA1, remapped from TIM5_CH2 to the unused TIM2_CH2, marked ALARM); it costs the addressable-LED-strip output, no servo/motor output, and keeps the onboard status LED. Board ID is inherited (Holybro-KakuteF4-Wing). For KakuteF4-Wing-Buzz, wire a passive buzzer to the LED pad — see the board's Readme.md.

Four more variants (v2.1) use the same LED-pad trick on boards whose buzzer output has no free timer, so stock can only beep at one pitch:

Variant Track Tone pad Timer Gives up
AtomRCF405NAVI-Buzz light LED pad next to SBUS (PB7) TIM4 LED strip (output 9)
TBS_LUCID_H7_OEM-Buzz full S13/LED (PA8) TIM1 LED strip (output 13)
CoreWingF405WingV2-Buzz light LED pad (PA8) TIM1 output 12 (plain PWM; output 11 moves to TIM12)
CoreWingF405MiniV2-Buzz light LED pad (PA8) TIM1 output 12 (plain PWM; output 11 moves to TIM12)

Motor and servo outputs are unchanged and the board IDs are inherited, so the .apj flashes as a normal update. Wire a passive piezo from the pad to GND. The stock buzzer output still works too; set NTF_BUZZ_PIN -1 if an active buzzer on it beeps over the tunes. On the Lucid, an existing setup keeps SERVO13_FUNCTION 120 from stock: set it to 0 (output 13 no longer exists, so it does nothing either way). On the CoreWings the LED pad never ran an LED strip in ArduPilot (no DMA stream is left for TIM1), so the variants lose only a spare PWM output. CoreWingF405MiniV2-Buzz drops the W from the stock name because ArduPilot limits board names to 23 characters.

Every -Buzz board ships next to its stock board in the same release, so anyone who wants the LED pad (for an LED strip or an output) flashes the plain one: AtomRCF405NAVI, TBS_LUCID_H7_OEM, CoreWingF405WingV2, CoreWingF405WMiniV2.

The comparable stock-upstream H7 board MatekH743-bdshot (Matek H743-WING, bidirectional DShot) is not a fork *-Buzz variant: it already carries an onboard buzzer (GPIO single-tone on PA15, since bidirectional DShot claims the TIM2 timer the non-bdshot base uses for a multi-tone ALARM), so no external buzzer wiring is needed. It shipped as a light asset through v0.2-beta; as of v0.3-beta it ships on the full track only (full-v0.3-beta) — the light H7 slot is now filled by KakuteH7-Wing.

Hardware requirements

  • A passive buzzer — a bare piezo or a magnetic passive buzzer. Do not use an active buzzer: it has a fixed internal oscillator and can only switch on/off, so it cannot reproduce the pitched tunes.
  • Recommended: an LS3040 passive piezo (~4 kHz resonance, rated 2 mA, 1–30 V). Its draw is well under the MCU pin limit, so it wires straight to the pad — no transistor, no diode (a piezo is capacitive, not inductive).
  • For a louder or magnetic buzzer: a small NPN transistor (2N2222 / S8050 / MMBT2222) or a logic-level N-MOSFET, plus a 1 kΩ base resistor (~100 Ω for a MOSFET gate), a 10 kΩ base/gate pull-down to GND, and — for a magnetic (coil) buzzer only — a 1N4148 flyback diode.
  • Signal pad: S11 (PB15). Power the buzzer high side / transistor stage from the 5 V servo rail (confirm the BEC feeds it) and GND. This costs servo output 11; outputs 1–10 and 12 (WS2812 LED) remain.

Wiring

Direct-drive passive piezo (recommended — e.g. LS3040):

S11 (PB15) ------[ LS3040 piezo ]------ GND

Polarity does not matter; a bare piezo needs no transistor and no diode. Driven off the 3.3 V pin swing it is a little quieter than its rated 80 dB but normally plenty audible.

Magnetic passive buzzer, or a louder piezo (transistor-driven):

5V (servo rail) ---+----------------+
                   |                |
              [ buzzer ]        1N4148  (band/cathode -> 5V)
                   |                |
                   +----------------+
                   |
               collector
S11 (PB15) -[1k]- base    NPN (2N2222 / S8050)
               emitter
                   |
         [10k] ----+   (base->GND pull-down: keeps it silent at boot)
                   |
                  GND

Omit the 1N4148 for a bare piezo (no coil to snub). The board leaves the stock active buzzer on PC15 in place — ignore it, or remove HAL_BUZZER_PIN from the hwdef if you don't want two noise-makers. Full notes and wiring photos live in the board's Readme.md.

v0.2-beta fleet change vs v0.1-beta: - Added: MatekF405-STD — a standard (non-bdshot) alternative in the F4 lineup, comfortable ~47 KB free headroom. - Dropped: LongBowF405WING (was unmeasured in v0.1-beta) and KakuteH7-Wing (2 MB H7 board, outside the "tight 1 MB F4" focus of the light variant).

Post-v0.2-beta fleet addition: - Added: omnibusf4pro (Omnibus F4 Pro) — user-requested. A stock upstream 1 MB F405 FPV flight controller (MPU6000/BMI270 IMU, BMP280 baro, onboard OSD), so no fork hwdef work was needed — it already pulls in minimize_fpv_osd.inc. Measured 41.6 KB free on the light variant (940,436 B of 1 MB used), right in the middle of the F4 fleet's headroom band. Shipped as a light-release asset alongside the boards above.

v0.3-beta fleet change vs v0.2-beta: - Serial numbering restored to SERIALn == UARTn on MatekF405-TE-bdshot, MatekF405-STD, and omnibusf4pro (see the serial-port section above). - Re-added: KakuteH7-Wing — the 2 MB H7 board dropped from the light fleet at v0.2-beta is back as a light asset (105.3 KB free), so it can be pulled from either track; it has ample flash for both variants. - Now full-only: MatekH743-bdshot — the other H7 board no longer ships as a light asset; it lives on full-v0.3-beta.

v1.0 fleet change vs v0.3-beta: - Added: MatekF765-Wing (Matek F765-WING, F7 / 2 MB) — the first F7 board in either fleet, shipped on both tracks (full-v1.0 and light-v1.0). Stock upstream board, no fork hwdef work needed. It has the most headroom of any board here: 521.0 KB free on full, 613.2 KB free on light. - Added (light only): AtomRCF405NAVI (AtomRC F405 Navi, 1 MB F4) — stock upstream FPV board, no fork hwdef work needed. 44.2 KB free on light, right in the middle of the F4 headroom band. 1 MB F4 → light-only (it overflows the full build, like the rest of the F4 fleet). - Plus code (OLC) is now compiled into every light board, including the 1 MB F4s (it was already on full and on the H7 light build). The ~2–3 KB cost trimmed each F4's free-flash figure above by roughly 1 KB versus v0.3-beta; every board still clears its ceiling (tightest is MatekF405-Wing-bdshot at 26.3 KB free).

v1.1 fleet change vs v1.0: - Removed from light: MatekF765-Wing (F7 / 2 MB) and KakuteH7-Wing (H7 / 2 MB). Both continue to ship on full, unchanged. Carrying 2 MB targets on a backend-stripped track never bought anything — the light variant exists to fit 1 MB F4 flash, and these boards were never constrained. Users on those two boards should flash the full asset. - The tracks are now cleanly split by MCU class: full = F7/H7 (3 boards), light = 1 MB F4 (9 boards). No board appears on both, so there is no longer a choice to get wrong. - No board was added, and no F4 board changed status. Light goes 11 → 9 purely by removing the two unconstrained targets.

v2.0 fleet change vs v1.1: - Rebased onto ArduPlane 4.7.1 (from 4.6.3). Both tracks are now built from one branch and one commit; the light configuration is picked by flash size. - Added to full: TBS_LUCID_H7_OEM (H7 / 2 MB, board ID 5255), XFLY-H743-bdshot (H7 / 2 MB, board ID 8888, the XFly VTOL kit FC) and MatekH7A3-Wing (H7A3 / 2 MB, board ID 1228), then after release TBS_LUCID_H7_WING_AIO (H7 / 2 MB, board ID 5254). Full goes 3 → 7 boards; light is unchanged at 9. - No board was removed and no board changed track. - Returning full boards gained 30–43 KB of free flash; light boards moved by −4.6 to +2.3 KB.

If a 1 MB F4 board overflows, the cheapest first trim is define HAL_SOARING_ENABLED 0 in that board's hwdef (Plane soaring is on by default and unused on twin-motor FPV wings; buys ~8–12 KB).

The OSD element draws once both planes have GPS lock; without lock it stays blank by design (see "Limitations" below).

Limitations / scope

  • GPS lock required on both planes for the element to draw. Your own plane needs ahrs.get_location() to compute bearing/distance, and the peer plane needs a fix to broadcast non-zero coords (a peer with lat=lon=alt=0 is treated as unhealthy). With no fix anywhere the OSD shows only a blinking letter ("A"); element switches to the full B→ 1.2km ↑15m form within ~2 s of both planes having lock.
  • One backend. Only MSP is implemented — no MAVLink, no proprietary radio backends. The mavlink message handler is a stub inherited from MustardTiger's design and currently does nothing.
  • No avoidance integration. Peers are displayed, not fed into AP_Avoidance — formation flight intentionally violates avoidance geometry, and ADS-B-style fan-out would have cost more flash than the whole feature.
  • Vertical arrow thresholds are fixed (25 m) — no parameter to tune them yet. Easy to add later if anyone asks.
  • No iNav-style "information-to-display" upstream channel. MSP2_SET_RADAR_ITD (0x100C) is reserved in the protocol header but not yet parsed.
  • No GCS "peer detected / lost" announcements in this release. t413's upstream PR #32333 adds STATUSTEXT events for peer state changes; we may cherry-pick that in a follow-up.

Quadplane / VTOL

Q_TRIM_PITCH is now knob-tunable

Q_TRIM_PITCH (the AHRS pitch trim used by QuadPlane's hover attitude reference) can be assigned to the in-flight tuning knob via TUNE_PARAM = 92 (TUNING_Q_TRIM_PITCH). Same shape as PTCH_TRIM_DEG being knob-tunable for fixed-wing.

  • TUNE_PARAM = 92, TUNE_CHAN = <RC channel>, TUNE_RANGE = <max-multiplier>
  • Active only when QuadPlane is enabled
  • OSD OSDx_TUNED_PN / OSDx_TUNED_PV display the live value

REQUIRED: Q_TRIM_PITCH must be non-zero before you engage the knob. Same multiplicative-knob caveat as PTCH_TRIM_DEG — a 0 seed means the knob has no effect. Set a small non-zero value first (e.g. 0.5 or -0.5), then re-centre with the selector switch.

VTOL AutoTrim — learn the hover level in QHOVER (RCx_OPTION = 182)

New in v2.0. If the aircraft slides one way in QHOVER with the sticks centred, the VTOL side's idea of "level" is off: a board mounted slightly tilted, a motor mount or boom not quite square, a surface catching prop wash. VTOL AutoTrim learns the correction in flight and stores it in the hover-only trims, so fixed-wing flight is unaffected.

  • Setup: RCx_OPTION = 182 on a two-position switch. This is the option number Copter uses for its AHRS AutoTrim; on Plane it is labelled VTOL AutoTrim.
  • Use: hover in QHOVER at a safe height in calm air, flip the switch HIGH (VTOL AutoTrim running), and hold the aircraft still over one spot with the sticks. Every 100 ms the roll and pitch you are holding move a little into the trim, so the stick correction you need shrinks toward centre over a few seconds. When the sticks sit centred and it no longer drifts, flip LOW to save (VTOL AutoTrim saved: roll x pitch y).
  • What it writes: Q_TRIM_ROLL (new) and Q_TRIM_PITCH, both ±10°. These rotate only the attitude reference the VTOL controller uses. AHRS_TRIM_X/Y, which the wing flies by, are never changed.
  • QHOVER only. Selecting it in any other mode, including QLOITER (whose lean also fights wind) and every fixed-wing mode, does nothing (VTOL AutoTrim: QHOVER only).
  • Cancel = undo. Leaving QHOVER, disarming or landing mid-run cancels it and restores the trims it started from (VTOL AutoTrim cancelled). A switch that is already HIGH when you enter QHOVER does not start a run; flip it LOW and HIGH again.
  • Stick deadzone: only corrections beyond the stick deadzone (RC1_DZ / RC2_DZ, 30 µs by default) reach the trim. A very gentle drift needs a deliberate correction to be learned.
  • Not on tailsitters, whose hover frame is pitched 90°; Q_TRIM_ROLL is ignored there.
  • Don't run it while the tuning knob drives Q_TRIM_PITCH (TUNE_PARAM = 92); the two would fight over the value.

Q_TRIM_ROLL can also be set by hand: positive rolls the aircraft right in VTOL flight, matching Q_TRIM_PITCH's positive = nose up.

Costs about 0.7 KB of flash.

Flight-tested on a KakuteH7-Wing quad-X VTOL: a full learn-and-save run in QHOVER. It refused to start in QLOITER, ran about 85 s in QHOVER and saved Q_TRIM_ROLL 0.4° / Q_TRIM_PITCH −4.1°, with AHRS_TRIM_X/Y untouched; the last ~50 s were hands-off at about 3 m with no drift. That run was all on one heading, and the hover has no wind estimate, so part of a learned pitch trim can be headwind. Learn it in calm air, or repeat on the opposite heading and compare.

Q_M_FRTB_RATIO — Tri-frame front/rear thrust balance

Scales the tail motor's thrust on Tri-class VTOL planes by 1 / Q_M_FRTB_RATIO. The two front motors are not changed.

  • Q_M_FRTB_RATIO = 1.0 (default) — unchanged from upstream behaviour
  • < 1.0 — the tail motor works harder, for a tail-heavy aircraft
  • > 1.0 — the tail motor works less, for a nose-heavy aircraft
  • Range: 0.5–2.0, step 0.001, Q_M_ subgroup. Values of 0 or below are ignored (treated as 1.0); other values outside the range are clamped.

What it actually changes. It is a feed-forward trim for an off-centre CG. The pitch controller already holds a tri level with a CG offset, by carrying the imbalance in its I-term. This parameter moves that correction into the mixer, so the I-term starts near zero and there is no pitch lurch at takeoff while it builds up. On a balanced aircraft, a value other than 1.0 creates the very imbalance it is meant to remove: in SITL, 0.8 or 1.25 on a balanced tri gave a 10–13° pitch transient on takeoff before the hover settled.

How to set it. Hover in QHOVER and look at the pitch I-term (PIQP.I in the log). Near zero means leave the ratio at 1.0. A steady offset means the CG is off:

  • PIQP.I steadily negative (the controller is holding the nose down against a sagging tail) → lower the ratio
  • PIQP.I steadily positive → raise the ratio

Change it in steps of about 0.05 and re-check. As a scale, on the SITL tri a ratio of 0.8 needed about +0.13 of I-term to cancel it, and 1.25 about −0.14.

The tail motor's share of pitch control is scaled the same way. The mixer accounts for the tail motor reaching full throttle earlier with a ratio below 1.0. With a reversed-pitch tri, the single motor is at the front and the same scaling applies to it.

Only the AP_MotorsTri backend uses this; ignored for quad / hex / oct frames.

Battery monitoring (AP_BattMonitor)

A larger toolbox of per-cell and Wh-based limits, plus an internal-resistance-aware consumed-Wh calculation.

New params

Param Purpose
BATTn_LOW_CV Low-cell-voltage failsafe threshold
BATTn_CRT_CV Critical-cell-voltage failsafe threshold
BATTn_CELL_VFULL Full-cell voltage (defines pack-full-when-plugged-in)
BATTn_CAPA_WH Pack capacity in Wh (alternative to mAh)
BATTn_LOW_WH Low-Wh failsafe
BATTn_CRT_WH Critical-Wh failsafe
BATTn_ARM_WH Minimum Wh required to arm
BATTn_CELL_DT_V Per-cell delta voltage for "full when plugged in"
BATTn_CELL_COUNT Manual override of detected cell count

Behaviour changes

  • consumed_wh now integrates with voltage_resting_estimate (was raw voltage). Reported Wh increases by ~10 % under load vs upstream — this is the energy delivered, internal-resistance losses included. A new consumed_wh_without_losses field preserves the upstream semantic for tools that need it.
  • BATTn_OPTIONS is now uint32 (was uint16) — bit 23 = Use_Wh_for_remaining_percent_calc, so the OSD battery % is computed off Wh instead of mAh when both CAPA_WH and the bit are set.

Stats (AP_Stats)

30+ tracked statistics vs upstream's 4 (boot count / flying time / run time / reset). Includes per-flight max airspeed/groundspeed, flight count, average distance from home, total energy consumed, etc. Used by the OSD stats grid above.

Schedule frequency increased 1 Hz → 100 Hz so peak values are captured accurately.

ℹ️ ArduPlane 4.7 added two statistics of its own, STAT_FLTCNT and STAT_DISTFLWN. They are not in this firmware — they duplicate the fork's STAT_FLT_CNT and STAT_TRAVEL_GND / STAT_TRAVEL_AIR and would have collided with their saved values. Your saved totals carry over.

TECS / throttle

Several control-loop ports from the fork plus tuning hooks. All have safe defaults — set them only if you actually need them.

Default changes

  • TECS_INTEG_GAIN default 0.3 → 0.4 (saved values preserved)

New params

Param Default Purpose
TECS_THR_FF_FILT 1.0 Throttle feed-forward low-pass-filter alpha (1.0 = no filter)
TECS_THR_FF_DAMP 1.0 Throttle FF dampening multiplier (1.0 = full FF)
RTL_SINK_MAX 0 Max sink rate in RTL (m/s, 0 = use TECS_SINK_MAX)
RTL_CLIMB_MAX 0 Max climb rate in RTL
AUTO_SINK_MAX 0 Max sink rate in AUTO
AUTO_CLIMB_MAX 0 Max climb rate in AUTO

TECS_THR_FF_FILT / TECS_THR_FF_DAMP are also exposed as a tuning set — TUNE_PARAM = 114 (TUNING_SET_TECS_THR_FF) sweeps both at once.

⚠️ This was 111 up to v1.1. ArduPlane 4.7 uses 111–113 for its own tuning sets, so the fork's set moved to 114. If you use it, change TUNE_PARAM (or TUNE_PARAM2 / TUNE_PARAM3) from 111 to 114 — left at 111 it now selects upstream's roll/pitch D+P set.

Behaviour changes

  • Throttle slew rate is now applied after the integrator sum, so the rate limit catches PD + FF + integrator together (was: rate limit applied only to PD+FF, then integrator added on top)
  • Throttle command in suppressed / non-auto-throttle phases is now written into TECS via set_throttle_demand(), giving a smooth hand-off when auto-throttle takes over (no THR_CRUISE snap)
  • TECS gliding integrates with the legacy set_gliding_requested_flag hook, shared with AP_Soaring

EKF / state estimator

EKF3-only. EKF2 is not compiled in.

Upstream already defaults HAL_NAVEKF2_AVAILABLE to 0 (in AP_AHRS_config.h, "EKF2 slated compiled out by default in 4.5, slated to be removed"), and ArduPlane 4.7.2 still does. This fork honours that default on every board it targets — neither the firmware binary nor the param list contains any EKF2 surface. Set AHRS_EKF_TYPE = 3 for normal operation (already the default).

Boards that explicitly re-enable EKF2 in their hwdef (e.g. upstream's CubeRed-EKF2 test target) are excluded from this fork's CI matrix.

Sensors

LightWare SF000/B rangefinder over I2C

The SF000/B microLiDAR speaks the same register protocol and uses the same default address (0x66) as LightWare's GRF-250/500, but upstream's RNGFNDx_TYPE = 48 driver only accepts sensors that name themselves GRF, so an SF000 on I2C was never detected. Type 48 now recognises it too and reads its 16-bit cm distance format.

Param Value
RNGFND1_TYPE 48 (LightWare-GRF-SF000-I2C)
RNGFND1_ADDR 102 (0x66)
RNGFND1_MIN / RNGFND1_MAX 0.2 / 48
RNGFND1_GRF_RET 1 (first return, filtered); default 0 is first return, raw
RNGFND1_GRF_ST minimum signal strength in percent on the SF000 (dB on the GRF); 0 = off
  • RNGFND1_GRF_RATE is ignored on the SF000; its update rate is set in LightWare Studio (48 Hz default, polled at 50 Hz).
  • No target in range reports just past RNGFND1_MAX (status OutOfRangeHigh) rather than dropping to NoData.
  • Wiring: the sensor's pins 2 and 4 must be joined as SDA. Its Startup mode must be "Wait for interface" or "I2C mode".
  • Boot shows LightWare SF000 detected (I2C) when it is found.

Telemetry

CRSF

  • Vehicle UID transmitted (for goggle OSD systems that key on it)
  • Relative altitude (above home) sent in addition to AMSL
  • CRSF system-info messages suppressed by default (cuts noise)

MSP / DJI

  • DJI FPV / HDZero goggles get attitude from the same source as the OSD horizon (VTOL-aware), so the numeric pitch/roll displays match the artificial horizon
  • MSP wind reported in km/h (was m/s)
  • Optional Link Quality output instead of raw RSSI
  • MSP_RC reports every RC channel the receiver delivers (up to 16), not just the first four. Since v2.1, with RC_32CH_ENABLE on, up to 18 (the Betaflight limit); see 32 RC channels and the 16-channel MSP output. Goggles and other MSP peers that display or act on AUX channels (switch positions, camera zoom) now see them, as they do on Betaflight; upstream issue #28276. The first four slots keep MSP's AERT order and their existing scaling. AUX channels are sent as received, with no trim or deadzone applied.

FrSky SPort passthrough

  • Airspeed bit now toggles between airspeed and groundspeed each frame
  • FRSKY_OPTIONS default flipped 0 → 1 to enable the alternation

Common

  • Throttle/scaled-RC values promoted int16 → float across all vehicle types (Plane/Copter/Rover/Sub/Blimp). Affects VFR_HUD.throttle, RC_Channel::get_control_in(), scripting gcs:get_hud_throttle(). Resolution improves; widening is source-compatible for callers that took int8/16 (implicit conversion).

Behaviour changes vs upstream — migration notes

These are the user-visible differences if you save params from a stock 4.7.2 build and then load this firmware:

Default change Effect
FLIGHT_OPTIONS 0 → 4096 (bit 12) New in v2.0. LOITER pitch-stick altitude control is on out of the box. See FLIGHT_OPTIONS bit 12. Upgrades keep their saved value.
RC_OPTIONS default is 544 (bits 5+9) Bit 20 (AUTO_SWITCH_TO_FBWA_WITH_STICKS) was removed in v1.1. Earlier builds defaulted to 1049120, where a 10 % stick bump anywhere in AUTO silently ended the mission. The stick takeover now exists only during a takeoff, as an auto-launch cancel, and needs no option bit. A stale bit 20 in saved parameters is ignored. See move sticks to cancel auto launch.
TECS_INTEG_GAIN 0.3 → 0.4 Slightly snappier altitude tracking.
OSD_OPTIONS default gains bit 18 (2-decimal vspeed) and bit 21 (1-decimal attitude) Cosmetic OSD-only; saved values preserved.
OSD_EFF_UNIT default Wh Was mAh in pre-2024 upstream; upstream now also Wh-default.
FRSKY_OPTIONS default 0 → 1 SPort passthrough rotates airspeed/groundspeed (FrSky users only).
consumed_wh integrates with voltage_resting_estimate Reported Wh ~10 % higher under load; use consumed_wh_without_losses for the old value.
AP_Stats scheduled at 100 Hz Peak-stat accuracy; CPU cost is negligible.
BATTn_OPTIONS is uint32 Bit 23 = use Wh for remaining %. Backwards-compat with uint16 saved values.
HAL_LANDING_DEEPSTALL_ENABLED (upstream: HAL_PROGRAM_SIZE_LIMIT_KB > 1024) → 0 Deepstall landing compiled out; mechanically incompatible with ELEVATOR_DIFF. Per-board hwdef can opt back in.
MANUAL mode now applies FWD_BAT_VOLT_* throttle voltage compensation Pilot's throttle stick maps to consistent thrust as battery sags. Set RC_OPTIONS bit 22 (PLANE_DISABLE_MAN_BAT_COMP) to opt back into upstream's pure-passthrough behaviour. Only takes effect if FWD_BAT_VOLT_MIN/MAX are configured (non-zero).

| Flight mode 26 is Course Hold, not upstream's AUTOLAND | AUTOLAND is compiled out. Use RTL_AUTOLAND + DO_LAND_START (with LAND_WIND_BIAS) for automatic landings. | | STAT_FLTCNT / STAT_DISTFLWN not present | The fork's own flight-count and distance statistics are used instead. |

Upgrading from v1.1 (ArduPlane 4.6.3 base)

v2.0 moved the fork from ArduPlane 4.6.3 to 4.7.1. Don't reset your parameters before upgrading — old values are converted on the first boot of v2.0, and a board that was wiped first has nothing to convert.

Converted automatically on first boot:

Was (v1.1) Now (v2.0) Note
ARMING_CHECK ARMING_SKIPCHK Inverted meaning: now a mask of checks to skip. 0 = run all checks.
SYSID_THISMAV / SYSID_MYGCS MAV_SYSID / MAV_GCS_SYSID
SYSID_ENFORCE, TELEM_DELAY MAV_OPTIONS, MAV_TELEM_DELAY
MAVLink bits of SERIALn_OPTIONS MAVn_OPTIONS
Q_ANGLE_MAX (centidegrees) Q_A_ANGLE_MAX (degrees)
Q_A_SLEW_YAW, Q_A_ACCEL_R/P/Y_MAX Q_A_RATE_WPY_MAX, Q_A_ACC_R/P/Y_MAX (deg/s, deg/s²)
QuadPlane position, pilot-speed and landing speeds (cm/s) same parameters in m/s, some renamed (Q_PILOT_SPD_UP, Q_WP_SPD, …)
Q_P_JERK_NE / Q_P_JERK_D Q_P_NE_JERK / Q_P_D_JERK value kept
EK3_MAX_FLOW EK3_FLOW_MAX
RNGFNDn_MIN_CM / RNGFNDn_MAX_CM / RNGFNDn_GNDCLEAR (cm) RNGFNDn_MIN / RNGFNDn_MAX / RNGFNDn_GNDCLR (metres) e.g. TFmini RNGFND1_MAX_CM 1200 becomes RNGFND1_MAX 12
CAM_RC_* (RunCam) CAM2_RC_* RunCam control is now camera 2 (CAM2_TYPE 8), set up automatically when a RunCam serial port or CAM_RC_TYPE was configured
GLIDE_SLOPE_MIN / GLIDE_SLOPE_THR ALT_SLOPE_MIN / ALT_SLOPE_MAXHGT renamed only; value kept
fork: LAND_WIND_STRICT, VEHICLE_UID, TKOFF_THR_IDLE same names storage moved because 4.7 reused the old slots; values carried over

Needs a manual change:

  • Parameter files (.parm) you load by hand are not converted. Update old names in them to the 4.7 names before loading, or load them on v1.1 first and upgrade afterwards.
  • FS_SHORT_TIMEOUT is gone (upstream). The short failsafe now starts when RC is declared lost, set by the new RC_FS_TIMEOUT (default 1 s; FS_SHORT_TIMEOUT defaulted to 1.5 s).
  • MAVLink stream rates moved from SRn_* to MAVn_* parameters. If your telemetry radio or Yaapu setup relied on custom stream rates, re-check them.
  • TECS feed-forward tuning set: TUNE_PARAM 111 → 114 (see TECS / throttle).
  • TKOFF_THR_IDLE is whole percent (see TKOFF_THR_IDLE).
  • MatekF765-Wing and KakuteH7-Wing: serial ports renumbered so SERIALn matches the TXn/RXn pad. Any SERIALn_* or BRD_SER1_RTSCTS value you set yourself must be moved to the port's new number; ports left on defaults follow automatically. See Serial port numbering.

Also changed by ArduPlane 4.7: ATC_INPUT_TC / Q_A_INPUT_TC defaults are lower; LOG_MAV_RATEMAX defaults to 10; HWSTATUS, MOUNT_CONFIGURE / MOUNT_CONTROL and HIL_GPS MAVLink messages are gone and RANGEFINDER is no longer sent by default (use DISTANCE_SENSOR); External AHRS, generator, KDECAN, Robotis and Volz support is no longer built for 2 MB boards. The full list is in ArduPlane's release notes.

Deliberately not included

Items evaluated and deliberately skipped, with reasoning:

  • Upstream 4.7 AUTOLAND flight mode — its number (26) is Course Hold here, and it picks the landing direction from the takeoff heading rather than the current wind; the fork's RTL_AUTOLAND + LAND_WIND_BIAS + RTL Autoland Commit path covers the same need
  • Angle-control-as-PID rewrite — large architectural risk; sticking with upstream's controllers
  • Throttle curves — upstream now has its own
  • Stick-mixing removal entirely — keeping the param exposed is more discoverable than deleting it
  • Throttle-expo (fixed-wing) — interlocked with deferred TECS reconciliation work
  • Auto-throttle nudge rewrite — upstream already rewrote nudge (8aafe85f6f); needs reconciliation, not a parallel port
  • #164 Plane-only OSD element gating — namespace cleanup with no Plane-only benefit; this build targets Plane only

Documentation and tooling

Everything in this chapter is a tool you can use outside the firmware — parameter docs, a bitmask calculator, and transmitter scripts. They are collected here rather than scattered through the feature sections.

→ ArduPilot Tools collects the browser tools on one page: the searchable parameter list, the bitmask calculator, the QRTL Planner, the LAND_WIND_BIAS Explorer and a link to the TECS tuning helper. Everything runs in your browser.

Tool What it is for Where
ArduPilot Tools site The browser tools below plus the QRTL Planner (where a QRTL starts its glide and how low it gets), the LAND_WIND_BIAS Explorer (which DO_LAND_START an autoland picks, and why) and the Adaptive Pitch Trim Explorer (plots a pitch-trim curve from a .param or .bin) erwinquilloy.github.io/ardupilot-tools
Full parameter reference Every parameter this firmware exposes, with descriptions, units and ranges — your GCS ships upstream metadata and will not describe fork parameters below
Bitmask calculator Tick bits, copy out the integer — or paste a value back to see which bits are set. Knows this fork's bits below
TECS tuning helper Step-by-step TECS tuning from the transmitter, reading live telemetry — Ethos and EdgeTX below
Yaapu Course Hold pack Makes modes 26 (Course Hold) and 27 (Auto Trim) show a name and speak their cue on Yaapu telemetry below

The parameter reference and the bitmask calculator cover both release tracks — they are generated from the same source.

Full parameter reference

Machine-generated parameter metadata for this fork lives at docs/parameters/. It covers every parameter the firmware exposes — including every fork-added bit on FLIGHT_OPTIONS, RC_OPTIONS, OSD_OPTIONS, and so on.

👉 Browse the parameter reference

Click the link below to read the full HTML parameter reference in your browser — no download, no GitHub account:

  • Searchable: https://erwinquilloy.github.io/ardupilot-tools/parameters.html (filter by name or text; each parameter has its own link, e.g. parameters.html#LAND_WIND_BIAS)
  • https://raw.githack.com/erwinquilloy/ardupilot/master_custom_4.7.1/docs/parameters/Parameters.html

(raw.githack.com serves the HTML with the right Content-Type so your browser actually renders it. raw.githubusercontent.com would serve the same file as plain-text source code.)

Other formats

All six formats param_parse.py produces are committed in the same directory:

File Use case
apm.pdef.json Best for tooling — easy to parse in JS / Python
apm.pdef.xml Alternative structured format
Parameters.html Browsable HTML (rendered URLs above)
Parameters.md GitHub-rendered Markdown
Parameters.rst Sphinx-flavoured reStructuredText
ParametersLatex.rst Book-style RST tuned for LaTeX

For tooling that fetches the raw JSON / XML directly, use raw.githubusercontent.com (it serves the file's actual bytes with text/plain, which is what JSON/XML parsers expect):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erwinquilloy/ardupilot/master_custom_4.7.1/docs/parameters/apm.pdef.json

The directory's own README lists the fork-specific bitmask bits and the most useful params to bring up in a calculator UI.

Bitmask calculator

A self-contained HTML/JS bitmask calculator for this fork's parameter set. It loads the JSON above, lets you tick bits to compute the integer value (or paste a value to see which bits are set), and shows decimal / hex / binary representations. Runs entirely in your browser — no server, no analytics, no GitHub account needed.

👉 Open the calculator

Click a link below to use the calculator in your browser:

  • https://erwinquilloy.github.io/ardupilot-tools/bitmask-calculator.html
  • https://raw.githack.com/erwinquilloy/ardupilot/master_custom_4.7.1/docs/bitmask_calculator.html

raw.githack.com is a free public CDN — no account, no login. It just proxies GitHub raw files with the correct Content-Type so HTML renders instead of showing source code. The URLs always serve the latest committed version of the file from the named branch.

Computing or reverse-engineering a value

To compute a value: 1. Pick the param (e.g. FLIGHT_OPTIONS) from the dropdown. 2. Tick the bits you want. The decimal / hex / binary fields update live. 3. Hit "Copy" and paste into Mission Planner / MAVProxy / QGroundControl.

To reverse-engineer an existing value: type or paste the integer into the Value (decimal) field; the bit checkboxes will reflect which bits are set.

Inspired by Stavros' ArduPilot bitmask calculator; this version uses this fork's parameter set so the fork-added bits on FLIGHT_OPTIONS (18 / 21 / 22 / 23 / 24), RC_OPTIONS bits 21 / 22, the OSD_OPTIONS bits, etc. are visible without leaving the page.

Want it offline / want to host it yourself?

The page also accepts a local JSON file upload, so you can keep a copy on a tablet for the field:

curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erwinquilloy/ardupilot/master_custom_4.7.1/docs/bitmask_calculator.html
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erwinquilloy/ardupilot/master_custom_4.7.1/docs/parameters/apm.pdef.json

Open the HTML file in your browser, then in the "Source" dropdown pick Upload file… and point at the JSON.

TECS tuning helper (Ethos / EdgeTX)

→ erwinquilloy/Arduplane_TECS_tuning_helper_ETHOS_ETX

A Lua script/widget that walks you through tuning TECS from the transmitter, using live passthrough telemetry — no laptop at the field. It reads the aircraft's telemetry, prompts you for each step, and converts the results into ArduPlane parameter units (e.g. dm/s → kph) on the radio itself. The finished TECS values are shown on screen and written to /LOGS/tecs_<timestamp>.txt.

It runs as a loop: read the instruction for the next step, wait for you to get the aircraft into the required state or speed, then capture the relevant values. Each step is triggered by one configured switch. The run cannot be paused or aborted, but you can repeat it as often as you like.
Radios FrSky Ethos (X20S, X20, X18/X18S, Twin) and EdgeTX (RadioMaster TX16S mk2/mk3, Horus X10/X12, Taranis X9D/Q7)
Transport CRSF passthrough (Crossfire & ELRS) and FrSky SPort passthrough (R9, X/S-series, F.Port). The Ethos widget auto-detects; on EdgeTX pick it with the UseCRSF setting
Needs Passthrough telemetry already working — see the Telemetry chapter
Sounds Custom callout sounds ship in the repo's /SOUNDS/; full soundpacks at mf0o/OpenTX_soundpacks

A fork of mf0o's opentx_arduplane_tecs_tuning_helper, extended with an Ethos port and updated for ArduPlane 4.5+ parameter names — the design and workflow are mf0o's. Built on Yaapu's FrSky Telemetry Script.

ℹ️ Separate repository, not part of this firmware — nothing to flash. It is listed here because it is the companion tool for tuning the aircraft this firmware flies.

Yaapu Course Hold telemetry pack

Stock Yaapu's plane-mode table stops short of mode 26, so Course Hold draws as a blank chip with no audio cue, and Auto Trim (mode 27) has no entry at all, which stops the Yaapu script. Drop-in files fix both: Tools/yaapu-coursehold/ in this repo, also attached to every release as plane.lua + coursehold.wav + autotrim.wav so you do not need to clone anything. Full install instructions — including the EdgeTX widget sound path, which is not the one you would guess — are in that directory's README and in the Course Hold flight-mode section.

Branch / repository layout

  • master_custom_4.7.2 — mainline (this branch), on ArduPlane 4.7.2, from v2.1. Builds both release tracks: 1 MB boards get the light configuration automatically. All ongoing work goes here.
  • master_custom_4.7.1 — the ArduPlane 4.7.1 base (v2.0). Frozen reference.
  • master_custom_4.6.3 / master_custom_4.6.3_light — the previous ArduPlane 4.6.3 base (full and light variants, releases up to v1.1). Frozen reference.
  • master_custom — legacy 2022-era fork from upstream 4.3.0-dev. Frozen reference, do not develop on it.
  • legacy-pre-rebase-2026 — tag pointing at the last commit of the legacy mainline.

Releases: two per-board tracks built from the same commit — full-v2.0 (F7 / H7 / 2 MB boards) and light-v2.0 (1 MB F4 boards). Each asset is <board>_plane_bin_<track>-<tag>_.zip with the 4 build products (arduplane, .apj, .bin, _with_bl.hex).

This README as a web page: python3 Tools/scripts/build_readme_html.py README_CUSTOM.html writes a single-file HTML copy with the outline in a side panel (needs pip install markdown). It is published on the ArduPilot Tools site with each release.
